16.336.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
tato gacchenmahādevi goṣpadaṃ tīrthamuttamam ..
yatra śrāddhaṃ naraḥ kṛtvā gayāsaptaguṇaṃ phalam..
labhate nātra saṃdeho yadi śraddhā dṛḍhā bhavet .. 1 ..
16.336.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
ततो गच्छेन्महादेवि गोष्पदं तीर्थमुत्तमम् ..
यत्र श्राद्धं नरः कृत्वा गयासप्तगुणं फलम्..
लभते नात्र संदेहो यदि श्रद्धा दृढा भवेत् .. 1 ..
16.336.m: Īśvara said: / Then, O great goddess, one should go to the excellent sacred ford Goṣpada, / where, having performed a śrāddha, a man obtains seven times the fruit of Gayā; / there is no doubt about this, if his faith is firm;

16.336.s: yatra śrāddhaṃ pṛthuḥ kṛtvā pitaraṃ pāpayonitaḥ .. uddadhāra mahādevi venaṃnāma mahāprabhum .. .. 2 ..
16.336.d: यत्र श्राद्धं पृथुः कृत्वा पितरं पापयोनितः .. उद्दधार महादेवि वेनंनाम महाप्रभुम् .. .. 2 ..
16.336.m: where Pṛthu, having performed a śrāddha, delivered his father from a sinful womb, / O great goddess, the mighty lord named Vena.

16.336.s:
.. devyuvāca .. ..
kasminsthāne sthitaṃ tīrthamutpattistasya kīdṛśī ..
kathaṃ sa venarājo vā uddhṛtaḥ pāpayonitaḥ .. 3 ..
16.336.d:
.. देव्युवाच .. ..
कस्मिन्स्थाने स्थितं तीर्थमुत्पत्तिस्तस्य कीदृशी ..
कथं स वेनराजो वा उद्धृतः पापयोनितः .. 3 ..
16.336.m: The goddess said: / In which place is this sacred ford situated, and of what kind is its origin? / Or how was that king Vena delivered from a sinful womb?

16.336.s:
gayāsaptaguṇaṃ puṇyaṃ kathaṃ tatra prajāyate ..
śrāddhasya kiṃ vidhānaṃ tu ke maṃtrāstatra ke dvijāḥ ..
etanme kautukaṃ deva yathāvadvaktumarhasi .. 4 ..
16.336.d:
गयासप्तगुणं पुण्यं कथं तत्र प्रजायते ..
श्राद्धस्य किं विधानं तु के मंत्रास्तत्र के द्विजाः ..
एतन्मे कौतुकं देव यथावद्वक्तुमर्हसि .. 4 ..
16.336.m: How is merit seven times greater than Gayā produced there? / What is the rule for the śrāddha, what are the mantras there, and who are the twice-born? / You ought to explain this curiosity of mine properly, O god.

16.336.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
idaṃ rahasyaṃ deveśi yattvayā paripṛcchitam..
aprakāśyamidaṃ tīrthamasminpāpayuge priye .. 5 ..
16.336.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
इदं रहस्यं देवेशि यत्त्वया परिपृच्छितम्..
अप्रकाश्यमिदं तीर्थमस्मिन्पापयुगे प्रिये .. 5 ..
16.336.m: Īśvara said: / This is a secret, O ruler of the gods, that has been asked by you. / This sacred ford is not to be revealed in this sinful age, O dear one.

16.336.s:
tathāpi saṃpravakṣyāmi tava snehātsureśvari ..
na pāpina idaṃ brūyānnaiva tarkaratāya vai .. 6 ..
16.336.d:
तथापि संप्रवक्ष्यामि तव स्नेहात्सुरेश्वरि ..
न पापिन इदं ब्रूयान्नैव तर्करताय वै .. 6 ..
16.336.m: Nevertheless, I shall tell it fully out of affection for you, O ruler of the gods. / One must not speak this to a sinner, nor indeed to one devoted to dry reasoning,

16.336.s:
na nāstikāya deveśi na suvarṇetarāya ca ..
asti devi mahāsiddhā puṇyā nyaṃkumatī nadī .. 7 ..
16.336.d:
न नास्तिकाय देवेशि न सुवर्णेतराय च ..
अस्ति देवि महासिद्धा पुण्या न्यंकुमती नदी .. 7 ..
16.336.m: nor to an atheist, O ruler of the gods, nor to one who is not of good caste. / O goddess, there is the greatly accomplished, sacred river Nyaṅkumatī,

16.336.s:
maryādārthaṃ mayā''nītā kṣetrasyāsya maheśvari..
saṃsthitā pāpaśamanī parṇādityācca dakṣiṇe.. 8 ..
16.336.d:
मर्यादार्थं मया'ऽनीता क्षेत्रस्यास्य महेश्वरि..
संस्थिता पापशमनी पर्णादित्याच्च दक्षिणे.. 8 ..
16.336.m: brought by me for the boundary of this sacred field, O great goddess. / Situated [there], destroying sins, to the south of Parṇāditya,

16.336.s:
nārāyaṇagṛhātsaumye nātidūre vyavasthitā..
tasyā madhye mahādevi tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam .. 9 ..
16.336.d:
नारायणगृहात्सौम्ये नातिदूरे व्यवस्थिता..
तस्या मध्ये महादेवि तीर्थं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम् .. 9 ..
16.336.m: and situated not very far to the north of the dwelling of Nārāyaṇa. / In the middle of it, O great goddess, is a sacred ford renowned in the three worlds,

16.336.s:
goṣpadaṃ nāma vikhyātaṃ koṭipāpaharaṃ nṛṇām..
goṣpadasya samīpe tu nātidūre vyavasthitaḥ .. 7.1.336.10 ..
16.336.d:
गोष्पदं नाम विख्यातं कोटिपापहरं नृणाम्..
गोष्पदस्य समीपे तु नातिदूरे व्यवस्थितः .. 7.1.336.10 ..
16.336.m: known by the name Goṣpada, which removes ten million sins of men. / Near Goṣpada, indeed not very far away, is stationed

16.336.s:
ananto nāma nāgendraḥ svayaṃbhūto dharātale ..
tasya tīrthasya rakṣārthaṃ viṣṇunā sanniyojitaḥ .. 11 ..
16.336.d:
अनन्तो नाम नागेन्द्रः स्वयंभूतो धरातले ..
तस्य तीर्थस्य रक्षार्थं विष्णुना सन्नियोजितः .. 11 ..
16.336.m: the king of serpents named Ananta, self-manifest on the surface of the earth, / appointed by Viṣṇu for the protection of that sacred ford.

16.336.s:
kāṃkṣaṃti pitaraḥ putrānnarakādatibhīravaḥ ..
gaṃtā yo goṣpade putraḥ sa nastrātā bhaviṣyati ..
goṣpade ca sutaṃ dṛṣṭvā pitṝṇāmutsavo bhavet .. 12 ..
16.336.d:
कांक्षंति पितरः पुत्रान्नरकादतिभीरवः ..
गंता यो गोष्पदे पुत्रः स नस्त्राता भविष्यति ..
गोष्पदे च सुतं दृष्ट्वा पितॄणामुत्सवो भवेत् .. 12 ..
16.336.m: Exceedingly terrified of hell, ancestors yearn for sons: / ‘The son who will go to Goṣpada, he will be our saviour.’ / Seeing a son at Goṣpada, a festival takes place for the ancestors:

16.336.s:
padbhyāmapi jalaṃ spṛṣṭvā asmabhyaṃ kiṃ na dāsyati ..
api syātsa kule'smākaṃ yo no dadyājjalāṃjalim ..
prabhāsakṣetramāsādya goṣpade tīrtha uttame .. 13 ..
16.336.d:
पद्भ्यामपि जलं स्पृष्ट्वा अस्मभ्यं किं न दास्यति ..
अपि स्यात्स कुलेऽस्माकं यो नो दद्याज्जलांजलिम् ..
प्रभासक्षेत्रमासाद्य गोष्पदे तीर्थ उत्तमे .. 13 ..
16.336.m: ‘Touching the water even with his feet, will he not give [an offering] to us? / Might there be one in our family who will offer us a handful of water, / having reached Prabhāsakṣetra, at the excellent sacred ford Goṣpada?

16.336.s:
api syātsa kule'smākaṃ khaḍgamāṃsena yaḥ sakṛt ..
śrāddhaṃ kuryātprayatnena kālaśākena vā punaḥ .. 14 ..
16.336.d:
अपि स्यात्स कुलेऽस्माकं खड्गमांसेन यः सकृत् ..
श्राद्धं कुर्यात्प्रयत्नेन कालशाकेन वा पुनः .. 14 ..
16.336.m: Might there be one in our family who will diligently perform a śrāddha once / with the flesh of a rhinoceros, or else with black greens?

16.336.s:
api syātsa kule'smākaṃ goṣpade dattadīpakaḥ ..
ākalpakālikā dīptistenā'smākaṃ bhaviṣyati .. 15 ..
16.336.d:
अपि स्यात्स कुलेऽस्माकं गोष्पदे दत्तदीपकः ..
आकल्पकालिका दीप्तिस्तेनाऽस्माकं भविष्यति .. 15 ..
16.336.m: Might there be one in our family who offers a lamp at Goṣpada? / Through that, light will belong to us lasting for an entire kalpa.’

16.336.s:
goṣpade cānnaśatā yaḥ pitarastena putriṇaḥ ..
dinamekamapi sthitvā punātyāsaptamaṃ kulam .. .. 16 ..
16.336.d:
गोष्पदे चान्नशता यः पितरस्तेन पुत्रिणः ..
दिनमेकमपि स्थित्वा पुनात्यासप्तमं कुलम् .. .. 16 ..
16.336.m: And the ancestors of one whose food is offered at Goṣpada are truly blessed with sons. / Remaining [there] even for a single day, one purifies one's family up to the seventh generation.

16.336.s:
piṇḍaṃ dadyācca pitrāderātmano'pi svayaṃ naraḥ ..
piṇyākeṃgudakenāpi tena mucyedvarānane .. 17 ..
16.336.d:
पिण्डं दद्याच्च पित्रादेरात्मनोऽपि स्वयं नरः ..
पिण्याकेंगुदकेनापि तेन मुच्येद्वरानने .. 17 ..
16.336.m: A man should offer a piṇḍa for his father and others, and even for himself by himself, / even with oil-cake or inguda fruits; through that he is liberated, O fair-faced lady.

16.336.s:
brahmajñānena kiṃ yogairgograhe maraṇena kim ..
kiṃ kurukṣetravāsena goṣpade yadi gacchati .. 18 ..
16.336.d:
ब्रह्मज्ञानेन किं योगैर्गोग्रहे मरणेन किम् ..
किं कुरुक्षेत्रवासेन गोष्पदे यदि गच्छति .. 18 ..
16.336.m: What is the use of the knowledge of Brahman, what of yogas, what of dying in the recapture of cows, / what of dwelling in Kurukṣetra, if one goes to Goṣpada?

16.336.s:
sakṛttīrthābhigamanaṃ sakṛtpiṇḍaprapātanam ..
durllabhaṃ kiṃ punarnityamasmiṃstīrthe vyavasthitam.. 19 ..
16.336.d:
सकृत्तीर्थाभिगमनं सकृत्पिण्डप्रपातनम् ..
दुर्ल्लभं किं पुनर्नित्यमस्मिंस्तीर्थे व्यवस्थितम्.. 19 ..
16.336.m: Visiting the sacred ford once, dropping a piṇḍa once, / is difficult to attain; how much more so [the fruit of] staying constantly in this sacred ford!

16.336.s:
arddhakośaṃ tu tattīrthaṃ tadarddhārddhaṃ tu durllabham ..
tanmadhye śrāddhakṛtpuṇyaṃ gayāsaptaguṇaṃ labhet .. 7.1.336.20 ..
16.336.d:
अर्द्धकोशं तु तत्तीर्थं तदर्द्धार्द्धं तु दुर्ल्लभम् ..
तन्मध्ये श्राद्धकृत्पुण्यं गयासप्तगुणं लभेत् .. 7.1.336.20 ..
16.336.m: That sacred ford extends half a krośa, and half of that half is exceedingly difficult to attain. / The performer of a śrāddha in the middle of it obtains seven times the merit of Gayā.

16.336.s:
śrāddhakṛdgoṣpade yastu pitṝṇāmanṛṇo hi saḥ ..
padamadhye viśeṣeṇa kulānāṃ śatamuddharet .. 21 ..
16.336.d:
श्राद्धकृद्गोष्पदे यस्तु पितॄणामनृणो हि सः ..
पदमध्ये विशेषेण कुलानां शतमुद्धरेत् .. 21 ..
16.336.m: Whoever performs a śrāddha at Goṣpada becomes indeed free from debt to his ancestors. / Especially in the middle of the footprint, he delivers a hundred families.

16.336.s:
gṛhāccalitamātrasya goṣpade gamanaṃ prati ..
svargārohaṇasopānaṃ pitṝṇāṃ tu padepade .. 22 ..
16.336.d:
गृहाच्चलितमात्रस्य गोष्पदे गमनं प्रति ..
स्वर्गारोहणसोपानं पितॄणां तु पदेपदे .. 22 ..
16.336.m: The moment one sets out from home toward the Goṣpada, / at every step there is a stairway for the ancestors climbing to heaven.

16.336.s:
pāyasenaiva madhunā saktunā piṣṭakena ca ..
caruṇā taṃdulādyairvā piṃḍadānaṃ vidhīyate .. 23 ..
16.336.d:
पायसेनैव मधुना सक्तुना पिष्टकेन च ..
चरुणा तंदुलाद्यैर्वा पिंडदानं विधीयते .. 23 ..
16.336.m: The offering of rice balls is prescribed with milk-rice alone, or with honey, / with roasted barley meal, or with cakes, or with boiled sacrificial rice, grains, and so forth.

16.336.s:
gopracāre tu yaḥ piṇḍā ñchamīpatrapramāṇataḥ ..
kandamūlaphalādyairvā dattvā svargaṃ nayetpitṝn .. 24 ..
16.336.d:
गोप्रचारे तु यः पिण्डा ञ्छमीपत्रप्रमाणतः ..
कन्दमूलफलाद्यैर्वा दत्त्वा स्वर्गं नयेत्पितॄन् .. 24 ..
16.336.m: Whoever offers rice balls in the cow pasture, even the size of a śamī leaf, / or with edible roots, bulbs, and fruits, leads his ancestors to heaven.

16.336.s:
goṣpade piṇḍadānena yatphalaṃ labhate naraḥ ..
na tacchakyaṃ mayā vaktuṃ kalpakoṭiśatairapi .. 25 ..
16.336.d:
गोष्पदे पिण्डदानेन यत्फलं लभते नरः ..
न तच्छक्यं मया वक्तुं कल्पकोटिशतैरपि .. 25 ..
16.336.m: The fruit that a person obtains by offering a rice ball at the Goṣpada / cannot be told by me even in hundreds of millions of kalpas.

16.336.s:
athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi samyagyātrāvidhiṃ śubham ..
yātrāvidhānaṃ ca tathā samyakchraddhānvitā śṛṇu .. .. 26 ..
16.336.d:
अथातः संप्रवक्ष्यामि सम्यग्यात्राविधिं शुभम् ..
यात्राविधानं च तथा सम्यक्छ्रद्धान्विता शृणु .. .. 26 ..
16.336.m: Henceforth I shall describe fully the auspicious rule of pilgrimage. / Endowed with full faith, listen to the procedure for the pilgrimage:

16.336.s:
yadi tīrthaṃ naro gacchedgayāśrāddhaphalepsayā ..
tathāvidhavidhānena yātrā kuryādvicakṣaṇaḥ .. 27 ..
16.336.d:
यदि तीर्थं नरो गच्छेद्गयाश्राद्धफलेप्सया ..
तथाविधविधानेन यात्रा कुर्याद्विचक्षणः .. 27 ..
16.336.m: If a man goes to the sacred ford desiring the fruit of a Gayā śrāddha, / the wise man should perform the pilgrimage according to that procedure.

16.336.s:
brahmacārī śucirbhūtvā hastapādeṣu saṃyataḥ ..
śraddhāvānāstiko bhāvī gacchettīrthaṃ tataḥ sudhīḥ .. 28 ..
16.336.d:
ब्रह्मचारी शुचिर्भूत्वा हस्तपादेषु संयतः ..
श्रद्धावानास्तिको भावी गच्छेत्तीर्थं ततः सुधीः .. 28 ..
16.336.m: Observing celibacy, purified, with hands and feet restrained, / faithful, believing in the beyond, reverent, the wise man should then go to the sacred ford.

16.336.s:
na nāstikasya saṃsargaṃ tasmiṃstīrthe naraścaret ..
sarvopaskarasaṃyuktaḥ śrāddhārha dravyasaṃyutaḥ ..
gacchettīrthaṃ sādhusaṃgī gayāṃ manasi mānayan .. 29 ..
16.336.d:
न नास्तिकस्य संसर्गं तस्मिंस्तीर्थे नरश्चरेत् ..
सर्वोपस्करसंयुक्तः श्राद्धार्ह द्रव्यसंयुतः ..
गच्छेत्तीर्थं साधुसंगी गयां मनसि मानयन् .. 29 ..
16.336.m: A man should not associate with an unbeliever at that sacred ford; / equipped with all accessories, supplied with items fit for the śrāddha, / keeping company with the virtuous, meditating on Gayā in his mind, he should go to the sacred ford.

16.336.s:
evaṃ yastu dvijo gacchetpratigrahavivarjitaḥ ..
padepade'śvamedhasya phalaṃ prāpnotya saṃśayam.. 7.1.336.30 ..
16.336.d:
एवं यस्तु द्विजो गच्छेत्प्रतिग्रहविवर्जितः ..
पदेपदेऽश्वमेधस्य फलं प्राप्नोत्य संशयम्.. 7.1.336.30 ..
16.336.m: A twice-born man who proceeds thus, refusing to accept gifts, / attains without doubt the fruit of a horse sacrifice at every step.

16.336.s:
tatra snātvā nyaṃkumatyāṃ siddhaye pitṛmuktaye ..
snātvātha tarppaṇaṃ kuryāddevādīnāṃ yathāvidhi .. 31 ..
16.336.d:
तत्र स्नात्वा न्यंकुमत्यां सिद्धये पितृमुक्तये ..
स्नात्वाथ तर्प्पणं कुर्याद्देवादीनां यथाविधि .. 31 ..
16.336.m: Having bathed there in the Nyaṅkumatī for spiritual success and the ancestors' liberation, / and having bathed, he should then perform the libation to the gods and others according to rule:

16.336.s:
brahmādistaṃbaparyaṃtā devarṣi manumānavāḥ ..
tṛpyantu pitaraḥ sarve mātṛmātāmahādayaḥ .. 32 ..
16.336.d:
ब्रह्मादिस्तंबपर्यंता देवर्षि मनुमानवाः ..
तृप्यन्तु पितरः सर्वे मातृमातामहादयः .. 32 ..
16.336.m: “From Brahmā down to a clump of grass, gods, seers, manus, and men— / may all ancestors, beginning with mother and maternal grandfather, be satisfied!”

16.336.s:
evaṃ saṃtarpya vidhinā kṛtvā homādikaṃ naraḥ ..
śrāddhaṃ sapiṇḍakaṃ kuryātsvataṃtroktavidhānataḥ .. 33 ..
16.336.d:
एवं संतर्प्य विधिना कृत्वा होमादिकं नरः ..
श्राद्धं सपिण्डकं कुर्यात्स्वतंत्रोक्तविधानतः .. 33 ..
16.336.m: Having thus offered libations according to rule and having performed the fire offering and the like, / a man should perform the śrāddha with rice balls according to the procedure taught in the independent text.

16.336.s:
āmantrya brāhmaṇāṃstatra śāstrajāndoṣavarjitān ..
evaṃ kṛtopacārastu imaṃ mantramudīrayet .. 34 ..
16.336.d:
आमन्त्र्य ब्राह्मणांस्तत्र शास्त्रजान्दोषवर्जितान् ..
एवं कृतोपचारस्तु इमं मन्त्रमुदीरयेत् .. 34 ..
16.336.m: Inviting there brahmins who know the scriptures and are free from faults, / and having thus offered hospitability, he should utter this mantra:

16.336.s:
kavyavāḍanalaḥ somo yamaścaivāryamā tathā ..
agniṣvāttā barhiṣadaḥ somapāḥ pitṛdevatāḥ ..
āgacchantu mahābhāgā yuṣmābhī rakṣitā stviha .. 35 ..
16.336.d:
कव्यवाडनलः सोमो यमश्चैवार्यमा तथा ..
अग्निष्वात्ता बर्हिषदः सोमपाः पितृदेवताः ..
आगच्छन्तु महाभागा युष्माभी रक्षिता स्त्विह .. 35 ..
16.336.m: “O Kavyavāha fire, Soma, Yama, and Aryaman, / Agniṣvāttas, Barhiṣads, Somapas, ancestral deities! / O noble ones, guarded by you, let them come here:

16.336.s:
madīyāḥ pitaro ye ca kule jātāḥ sanābhayaḥ ..
teṣāṃ piṇḍapradātā'hamāgato'sminpitāmahāḥ .. 36 ..
16.336.d:
मदीयाः पितरो ये च कुले जाताः सनाभयः ..
तेषां पिण्डप्रदाताऽहमागतोऽस्मिन्पितामहाः .. 36 ..
16.336.m: Those who are my ancestors, born in this family, my kinsmen— / I have come here to offer rice balls to them, O grandfathers!”

16.336.s: evamuktvā mahādevi imaṃ mantramudīrayet .. 37 ..
16.336.d: एवमुक्त्वा महादेवि इमं मन्त्रमुदीरयेत् .. 37 ..
16.336.m: Having said this, O great goddess, he should utter this mantra:

16.336.s:
pitā pitāmahaścaiva tathaiva prapitāmahaḥ ..
mātā pitāmahī caiva tathaiva prapitāmahī .. 38 ..
16.336.d:
पिता पितामहश्चैव तथैव प्रपितामहः ..
माता पितामही चैव तथैव प्रपितामही .. 38 ..
16.336.m: “Father, paternal grandfather, and likewise great-grandfather, / mother, paternal grandmother, and likewise paternal great-grandmother,

16.336.s:
mātāmahaḥ pramātā ca tathā vṛddhapramātṛkaḥ ..
teṣāṃ piṃḍo mayā datto hyakṣayyamupatiṣṭhatām .. 39 ..
16.336.d:
मातामहः प्रमाता च तथा वृद्धप्रमातृकः ..
तेषां पिंडो मया दत्तो ह्यक्षय्यमुपतिष्ठताम् .. 39 ..
16.336.m: maternal grandfather, maternal great-grandfather, and elderly maternal great-great-grandfather: / to them a rice ball has been offered by me; may it remain inexhaustible!”

16.336.s:
oṃ namo bhānave bhartre'bjabhaumasomarū piṇe ..
evaṃ natvā'rcayitvā tu imāṃ stutimatho paṭhet .. 7.1.336.40 ..
16.336.d:
ओं नमो भानवे भर्त्रेऽब्जभौमसोमरू पिणे ..
एवं नत्वाऽर्चयित्वा तु इमां स्तुतिमथो पठेत् .. 7.1.336.40 ..
16.336.m: “Oṃ, homage to the Sun, the maintainer, who has the forms of the lotus, Mars, and the Moon.” / Having bowed and worshipped thus, he should then recite this praise:

16.336.s:
tatra goṣpadasāmīpye caruṇā suśṛtena ca ..
pitṝṇāmanāthānāṃ ca maṃtraiḥ piṃḍāṃśca nirvapet .. 41 ..
16.336.d:
तत्र गोष्पदसामीप्ये चरुणा सुशृतेन च ..
पितॄणामनाथानां च मंत्रैः पिंडांश्च निर्वपेत् .. 41 ..
16.336.m: There, near the Goṣpada, with well-cooked sacrificial rice, / he should offer rice balls with mantras for the helpless ancestors:

16.336.s:
asmatkule mṛtā ye ca gatiryeṣāṃ na vidyate ..
raurave cāṃdhatāmisre kālasūtre ca ye gatāḥ ..
teṣāmuddharaṇārthāya imaṃ piṃḍaṃ dadāmyaham .. .. 42 ..
16.336.d:
अस्मत्कुले मृता ये च गतिर्येषां न विद्यते ..
रौरवे चांधतामिस्रे कालसूत्रे च ये गताः ..
तेषामुद्धरणार्थाय इमं पिंडं ददाम्यहम् .. .. 42 ..
16.336.m: “Those who have died in our family and who have no goal, / and those who have gone to Raurava, Andhatāmisra, and Kālasūtra— / for their rescue I give this rice ball.

16.336.s:
anekayātanāsaṃsthāḥ pretalokeṣu ye gatāḥ ..
teṣāmuddharaṇārthāya imaṃ piṃḍaṃ dadāmyaham .. 43 ..
16.336.d:
अनेकयातनासंस्थाः प्रेतलोकेषु ये गताः ..
तेषामुद्धरणार्थाय इमं पिंडं ददाम्यहम् .. 43 ..
16.336.m: Those who dwell in manifold torments and have gone to the worlds of ghosts— / for their rescue I give this rice ball.

16.336.s:
paśuyonigatā ye ca ye ca kīṭasarī sṛpāḥ ..
athavā vṛkṣayonisthāstebhyaḥ piṃḍaṃ dadāmyaham ..44..
16.336.d:
पशुयोनिगता ये च ये च कीटसरी सृपाः ..
अथवा वृक्षयोनिस्थास्तेभ्यः पिंडं ददाम्यहम् ..44..
16.336.m: Those who have entered animal wombs, and those who are insects or reptiles, / or those who dwell in the womb of trees—to them I give this rice ball.

16.336.s:
asaṃkhyā yātanāsaṃsthā ye nītā yamaśāsakaiḥ..
teṣāmuddharaṇārthāya imaṃ piṃḍaṃ dadāmyaham .. 45 ..
16.336.d:
असंख्या यातनासंस्था ये नीता यमशासकैः..
तेषामुद्धरणार्थाय इमं पिंडं ददाम्यहम् .. 45 ..
16.336.m: Those who, dwelling in countless torments, were led away by the punishers of Yama— / for their rescue I give this rice ball.

16.336.s:
ye'bāṃdhavā bāṃdhavā ye ye'nyajanmani bāṃdhavāḥ ..
te sarve tṛptimāyāṃtu piṃḍenānena sarvadā .. 46 ..
16.336.d:
येऽबांधवा बांधवा ये येऽन्यजन्मनि बांधवाः ..
ते सर्वे तृप्तिमायांतु पिंडेनानेन सर्वदा .. 46 ..
16.336.m: Those who are not kinsmen, those who are kinsmen, and those who were kinsmen in another birth— / may all of them attain satisfaction forever through this rice ball.

16.336.s:
ye kecitpretarūpeṇa varttaṃte pitaro mama ..
te sarve tṛptimāyāṃtu piṃḍenānena sarvadā .. 47 ..
16.336.d:
ये केचित्प्रेतरूपेण वर्त्तंते पितरो मम ..
ते सर्वे तृप्तिमायांतु पिंडेनानेन सर्वदा .. 47 ..
16.336.m: Whosoever among my ancestors exist in the form of a ghost— / may all of them attain satisfaction forever through this rice ball.

16.336.s:
divyāṃtarikṣabhūmisthapitaro bāṃdhavādayaḥ ..
mṛtāścāsaṃskṛtā ye ca teṣāṃ piṃḍostu muktaye .. .. 48 ..
16.336.d:
दिव्यांतरिक्षभूमिस्थपितरो बांधवादयः ..
मृताश्चासंस्कृता ये च तेषां पिंडोस्तु मुक्तये .. .. 48 ..
16.336.m: Ancestors, kinsmen, and others dwelling in the celestial realm, mid-air, or earth, / and those who died without rites of passage—may the rice ball be for their liberation.

16.336.s:
pitṛvaṃśe mṛtā ye ca mātṛvaṃśe tathaiva ca ..
guruśvaśurabaṃdhūnāṃ ye cānye bāṃdhavā mṛtāḥ .. 49 ..
16.336.d:
पितृवंशे मृता ये च मातृवंशे तथैव च ..
गुरुश्वशुरबंधूनां ये चान्ये बांधवा मृताः .. 49 ..
16.336.m: Those who have died in the paternal lineage, and likewise in the maternal lineage, / and whatever other kinsmen of the guru, father-in-law, and relatives have died;

16.336.s:
ye me kule luptapiṃḍāḥ putradāravivarjitāḥ ..
kriyālopagatā ye ca jātyaṃdhāḥ paṃgavastathā .. 7.1.336.50 ..
16.336.d:
ये मे कुले लुप्तपिंडाः पुत्रदारविवर्जिताः ..
क्रियालोपगता ये च जात्यंधाः पंगवस्तथा .. 7.1.336.50 ..
16.336.m: those in my family who have lost their rice-ball offerings, who are without sons and wives, / who have suffered omission of rites, and likewise those born blind or lame;

16.336.s:
virūpā āmagarbhā ye'jñātā jñātāḥ kule mama ..
teṣāṃ piṃḍo mayā datto hyakṣayyamupatiṣṭhatām.. ..51..
16.336.d:
विरूपा आमगर्भा येऽज्ञाता ज्ञाताः कुले मम ..
तेषां पिंडो मया दत्तो ह्यक्षय्यमुपतिष्ठताम्.. ..51..
16.336.m: the deformed, the miscarried embryos, the unknown and the known in my family— / to them a rice ball has been offered by me; may it remain inexhaustible!

16.336.s:
pretatvātpitaro muktā bhavaṃtu mama śāśvatam ..
yatkiṃcinmadhusamiśraṃ gokṣīraṃ ghṛtapāyasam ..52..
16.336.d:
प्रेतत्वात्पितरो मुक्ता भवंतु मम शाश्वतम् ..
यत्किंचिन्मधुसमिश्रं गोक्षीरं घृतपायसम् ..52..
16.336.m: May my ancestors be freed forever from ghosthood!” / Whatever is mixed with honey, cow's milk, or ghee with milk-rice—

16.336.s:
akṣayyamupatiṣṭhettvattvasmiṃstīrthe tu goṣpade..
svādhyāyaṃ śrāvayettatra purāṇānyakhilānyapi .. 53 ..
16.336.d:
अक्षय्यमुपतिष्ठेत्त्वत्त्वस्मिंस्तीर्थे तु गोष्पदे..
स्वाध्यायं श्रावयेत्तत्र पुराणान्यखिलान्यपि .. 53 ..
16.336.m: may it remain inexhaustible from you at this sacred ford, the Goṣpada! / There he should recite the sacred study and all the Purāṇas,

16.336.s:
brahmaviṣṇvarkarudrāṇāṃ stavāni vividhāni ca..
aiṃdrāṇi somasūktāni pāvamānīśca śaktitaḥ .. .. 54 ..
16.336.d:
ब्रह्मविष्ण्वर्करुद्राणां स्तवानि विविधानि च..
ऐंद्राणि सोमसूक्तानि पावमानीश्च शक्तितः .. .. 54 ..
16.336.m: various hymns of praise to Brahmā, Viṣṇu, the Sun, and Rudra, / hymns to Indra, hymns to Soma, and purifying verses according to his capacity;

16.336.s:
bṛhadrathaṃtaraṃ tadvajjyeṣṭhasāma sarauravam..
tathaiva śāṃtikādhyāyaṃ madhubrāhmaṇameva ca ..55..
16.336.d:
बृहद्रथंतरं तद्वज्ज्येष्ठसाम सरौरवम्..
तथैव शांतिकाध्यायं मधुब्राह्मणमेव च ..55..
16.336.m: likewise the Bṛhat and Rathaṃtara, the Jyeṣṭhasāman along with the Raurava, / and likewise the peace chapter and the Madhubrāhmaṇa,

16.336.s:
maṃḍalaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ tatra prītakāri ca yatpunaḥ ..
viprāṇāmātmanaścaiva tatsarvaṃ samudīrayet..56..
16.336.d:
मंडलं ब्राह्मणं तत्र प्रीतकारि च यत्पुनः ..
विप्राणामात्मनश्चैव तत्सर्वं समुदीरयेत्..56..
16.336.m: the Maṇḍalabrāhmaṇa, and whatever else brings delight there / to the brahmins and to oneself—he should recite all of that.

16.336.s:
evaṃ nyaṃkumatīmadhye goṣpade tīrtha uttame ..
dattvā piṃḍāṃśca vidhivatpunarmaṃtramimaṃ paṭhet .. 57 ..
16.336.d:
एवं न्यंकुमतीमध्ये गोष्पदे तीर्थ उत्तमे ..
दत्त्वा पिंडांश्च विधिवत्पुनर्मंत्रमिमं पठेत् .. 57 ..
16.336.m: Having thus offered rice balls according to rule in the middle of the Nyaṅkumatī, at the excellent sacred ford Goṣpada, / he should again recite this mantra:

16.336.s:
sākṣiṇaḥ saṃtu me devā brahmādyā ṛṣipuṃgavāḥ ..
mayedaṃ tīrthamāsādya pitṝṇāṃ niṣkṛtiḥ kṛtā ..58..
16.336.d:
साक्षिणः संतु मे देवा ब्रह्माद्या ऋषिपुंगवाः ..
मयेदं तीर्थमासाद्य पितॄणां निष्कृतिः कृता ..58..
16.336.m: “May the gods, beginning with Brahmā, and the foremost seers be witnesses for me: / having reached this sacred ford, expiation for the ancestors has been made by me!

16.336.s:
āgato'smi idaṃ tīrthaṃ pitṛkārye surottamāḥ ..
bhavaṃtu sākṣiṇaḥ sarve muktaścāhamṛṇatrayāt.. 59 ..
16.336.d:
आगतोऽस्मि इदं तीर्थं पितृकार्ये सुरोत्तमाः ..
भवंतु साक्षिणः सर्वे मुक्तश्चाहमृणत्रयात्.. 59 ..
16.336.m: I have come to this sacred ford for ancestral rites, O best of gods; / may you all be witnesses, and may I be freed from the three debts!”

16.336.s:
evaṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya goṣpadaṃ tīrthamuttamam ..
viprebhyo dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā nadyāṃ piṃḍānvisarjayet .. 7.1.336.60 ..
16.336.d:
एवं प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य गोष्पदं तीर्थमुत्तमम् ..
विप्रेभ्यो दक्षिणां दत्त्वा नद्यां पिंडान्विसर्जयेत् .. 7.1.336.60 ..
16.336.m: Having thus circumambulated the excellent sacred ford Goṣpada, / having given priestly gifts to the brahmins, he should consign the rice balls into the river.

16.336.s:
godānaṃ tatra deyaṃ tu tadvatkṛṣṇājinaṃ priye ..
aṣṭakāsu ca vṛddhau ca gayāyāṃ mṛtavāsare .. 61 ..
16.336.d:
गोदानं तत्र देयं तु तद्वत्कृष्णाजिनं प्रिये ..
अष्टकासु च वृद्धौ च गयायां मृतवासरे .. 61 ..
16.336.m: A gift of a cow should be made there, and likewise a black antelope skin, my dear, / on the Aṣṭakā days, at a prosperity rite, at Gayā, and on the death anniversary.

16.336.s:
atra mātuḥ pṛthakchrāddhamanyatra patinā saha ..
vṛddhiśrāddhe tu mātrādi gayāyāṃ pitṛpūrvakam.. 62 ..
16.336.d:
अत्र मातुः पृथक्छ्राद्धमन्यत्र पतिना सह ..
वृद्धिश्राद्धे तु मात्रादि गयायां पितृपूर्वकम्.. 62 ..
16.336.m: Here the mother's śrāddha is performed separately, but elsewhere along with her husband; / in a prosperity śrāddha, the mother comes first, whereas at Gayā it begins with the father.

16.336.s:
gayāvadatraiva punaḥ śrāddhaṃ kāryaṃ narottamaiḥ ..
tasmādguptagayā proktā iyaṃ sā viṣṇunā svayam .. 63 ..
16.336.d:
गयावदत्रैव पुनः श्राद्धं कार्यं नरोत्तमैः ..
तस्माद्गुप्तगया प्रोक्ता इयं सा विष्णुना स्वयम् .. 63 ..
16.336.m: The śrāddha should be performed here by the best of men just as at Gayā; / therefore this was declared as Guptagayā by Viṣṇu himself.

16.336.s:
gaṃdhadānena gaṃdhāptiḥ saubhāgyaṃ puṣpadānataḥ ..
dhūpadānena rājyāptirdīptirdīpapradānataḥ .. 64 ..
16.336.d:
गंधदानेन गंधाप्तिः सौभाग्यं पुष्पदानतः ..
धूपदानेन राज्याप्तिर्दीप्तिर्दीपप्रदानतः .. 64 ..
16.336.m: By the gift of fragrant paste one obtains fragrance; good fortune comes from the gift of flowers; / by the gift of incense one obtains a kingdom; radiance comes from the offering of a lamp.

16.336.s:
dhvajadānātpāpahāniryātrākṛdbrahmalokabhāk ..
śrāddhapiṃḍaprado loke viṣṇurneṣyati vai pitṝn.. 65 ..
16.336.d:
ध्वजदानात्पापहानिर्यात्राकृद्ब्रह्मलोकभाक् ..
श्राद्धपिंडप्रदो लोके विष्णुर्नेष्यति वै पितॄन्.. 65 ..
16.336.m: By giving a banner, one is freed from sin; the pilgrim attains the world of Brahmā. / In this world, whoever offers funeral balls in the śrāddha, Viṣṇu will indeed lead his ancestors [to heaven]. (65)

16.336.s:
ekaṃ yo bhojayettatra brāhmaṇaṃ śaṃsitavratam..
gopracāre mahātīrthe koṭirbhavatibhojitā .. 66 ..
16.336.d:
एकं यो भोजयेत्तत्र ब्राह्मणं शंसितव्रतम्..
गोप्रचारे महातीर्थे कोटिर्भवतिभोजिता .. 66 ..
16.336.m: If one feeds even a single brahmin of commended vows there, / at the great tīrtha Gopracāra, it equals feeding ten million. (66)

16.336.s:
iti saṃkṣepataḥ proktastatra śrāddhavidhistava ..
atha te kathayiṣyāmi itihāsaṃ purātanam .. 67 ..
16.336.d:
इति संक्षेपतः प्रोक्तस्तत्र श्राद्धविधिस्तव ..
अथ ते कथयिष्यामि इतिहासं पुरातनम् .. 67 ..
16.336.m: Thus the rite of śrāddha there has been briefly spoken to you. / Now I will tell you an ancient history: (67)

16.336.s:
venasya rājñaścaritaṃ pṛthoścaiva mahātmanaḥ ..
yathā tatrābhavanmuktistasya cāṃḍālayonitaḥ ..
tatsarvaṃ śṛṇu deveśi samyakchraddhāsamānvitā .. 68 ..
16.336.d:
वेनस्य राज्ञश्चरितं पृथोश्चैव महात्मनः ..
यथा तत्राभवन्मुक्तिस्तस्य चांडालयोनितः ..
तत्सर्वं शृणु देवेशि सम्यक्छ्रद्धासमान्विता .. 68 ..
16.336.m: The deed of King Vena and of the great-souled Pṛthu, / how his liberation occurred there from a cāṇḍāla's womb. / Hear all of that, O Queen of the Gods, endowed with proper faith. (68)

16.336.s:
piśunāya na pāpāya nāśiṣyāyāhitāya ca ..
kathanīyamidaṃ puṇyaṃ nāvratāya kathaṃcana .. 69 ..
16.336.d:
पिशुनाय न पापाय नाशिष्यायाहिताय च ..
कथनीयमिदं पुण्यं नाव्रताय कथंचन .. 69 ..
16.336.m: This holy [account] must not be told to a slanderer, to a sinner, / nor to one who is not a pupil, nor to one who is hostile, nor in any way to one without vows. (69)

16.336.s:
svargyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ dhanyaṃ vedena saṃmitam ..
rahasyamṛṣibhiḥ proktaṃ śṛṇuyādyo'nasūyakaḥ .. 7.1.336.70 ..
16.336.d:
स्वर्ग्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं धन्यं वेदेन संमितम् ..
रहस्यमृषिभिः प्रोक्तं शृणुयाद्योऽनसूयकः .. 7.1.336.70 ..
16.336.m: Bestowing heaven, fame, and long life, bringing fortune, equal to the Veda, / this secret was declared by the seers; he who listens without malice, (70)

16.336.s:
yaścainaṃ śrāvayenmartyaḥ pṛtho rvainyasya saṃbhavam ..
brāhmaṇebhyo namaskṛtvā na sa śocetkṛtā'kṛte ..71..
16.336.d:
यश्चैनं श्रावयेन्मर्त्यः पृथो र्वैन्यस्य संभवम् ..
ब्राह्मणेभ्यो नमस्कृत्वा न स शोचेत्कृताऽकृते ..71..
16.336.m: and the mortal who recites this origin of Pṛthu, son of Vena, / having bowed to the brahmins, will not grieve over deeds done or left undone. (71)

16.336.s:
goptā dharmasya rājā'sau babhau cātrisamaprabhaḥ ..
atrivaṃśasamutpanno hyaṃgo nāma prajāpatiḥ .. 72 ..
16.336.d:
गोप्ता धर्मस्य राजाऽसौ बभौ चात्रिसमप्रभः ..
अत्रिवंशसमुत्पन्नो ह्यंगो नाम प्रजापतिः .. 72 ..
16.336.m: A protector of dharma, that king shone with splendour equal to Atri; / indeed, born in Atri's lineage, he was the Prajāpati named Aṅga. (72)

16.336.s:
tasya putro'bhavedveno nātyarthaṃ dhārmikastathā ..
jāto mṛtyusutāyāṃ vai sunīthāyāṃ prajāpatiḥ..73 ..
16.336.d:
तस्य पुत्रोऽभवेद्वेनो नात्यर्थं धार्मिकस्तथा ..
जातो मृत्युसुतायां वै सुनीथायां प्रजापतिः..73 ..
16.336.m: His son was Vena, who was not particularly righteous; / he was born to Sunīthā, the daughter of Mṛtyu, a Prajāpati. (73)

16.336.s:
samātāmaha doṣeṇa tena kālātmakānanaḥ ..
sa dharmaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā pāpabuddhirajāyata .. 74 ..
16.336.d:
समातामह दोषेण तेन कालात्मकाननः ..
स धर्मं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा पापबुद्धिरजायत .. 74 ..
16.336.m: Through that fault of his maternal grandfather, with a face like Death himself, / he set dharma aside and became one whose mind was bent on sin. (74)

16.336.s:
sthitimutthāpayāmāsa dharmopetāṃ sanātanīm ..
vedaśāstrāṇyatikramya hyadharma nirato'bhavat .. 75 ..
16.336.d:
स्थितिमुत्थापयामास धर्मोपेतां सनातनीम् ..
वेदशास्त्राण्यतिक्रम्य ह्यधर्म निरतोऽभवत् .. 75 ..
16.336.m: He abolished the eternal order endowed with dharma; / transgressing the Vedic scriptures, he devoted himself to unrighteousness. (75)

16.336.s:
niḥsvādhyāyavaṣaṭkārāḥ prajāstasminpraśāsati ..
ḍiṃḍimaṃ ghoṣayāmāsa sa rājā viṣaye svake .. 76 ..
16.336.d:
निःस्वाध्यायवषट्काराः प्रजास्तस्मिन्प्रशासति ..
डिंडिमं घोषयामास स राजा विषये स्वके .. 76 ..
16.336.m: While he ruled, his subjects were without Vedic study or the exclamation vaṣaṭ. / That king caused a drum to be proclaimed throughout his kingdom: (76)

16.336.s:
na dātavyaṃ na yaṣṭavyaṃ mayi rājyaṃ praśāsati ..
āsītpratijñā krūreyaṃ vināśe pratyupasthite .. 77..
16.336.d:
न दातव्यं न यष्टव्यं मयि राज्यं प्रशासति ..
आसीत्प्रतिज्ञा क्रूरेयं विनाशे प्रत्युपस्थिते .. 77..
16.336.m: ‘No gifts must be given, no sacrifice must be made, while I rule the kingdom!’ / Such was his cruel vow when his destruction was at hand. (77)

16.336.s:
ahamīḍyaśca pūjyaśca sarvayajñairdvijottamaiḥ ..
mayi yajñā vidhātavyā mayi hotavyamityapi ..78..
16.336.d:
अहमीड्यश्च पूज्यश्च सर्वयज्ञैर्द्विजोत्तमैः ..
मयि यज्ञा विधातव्या मयि होतव्यमित्यपि ..78..
16.336.m: ‘I alone am to be praised and worshipped with all sacrifices by the best of the twice-born! / Sacrifices must be offered to me, and oblations poured unto me!’ (78)

16.336.s:
tamatikrāṃtamaryādaṃ prajāpīḍanatatparam ..
ūcurmaharṣayaḥ kruddhā marīcipramukhāstadā ..79..
16.336.d:
तमतिक्रांतमर्यादं प्रजापीडनतत्परम् ..
ऊचुर्महर्षयः क्रुद्धा मरीचिप्रमुखास्तदा ..79..
16.336.m: Seeing that he had transgressed boundaries and was intent on oppressing his subjects, / the enraged great seers, led by Marīci, said to him then: (79)

16.336.s:
mā'dharmaṃ vena kārṣīstvaṃ naiṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ ..
atrervaṃśe prasūto'si prajāpatirasaṃśayam .. 7.1.336.80 ..
16.336.d:
माऽधर्मं वेन कार्षीस्त्वं नैष धर्मः सनातनः ..
अत्रेर्वंशे प्रसूतोऽसि प्रजापतिरसंशयम् .. 7.1.336.80 ..
16.336.m: ‘Do not commit unrighteousness, O Vena! This is not the eternal dharma! / You are born in the lineage of Atri, without doubt a Prajāpati. (80)

16.336.s:
pālayiṣye prajāśceti pūrvaṃ te samayaḥ kṛtaḥ ..
tāṃstathāvādinaḥ sarvānbrahmarṣīnabravīttadā .. 81 ..
16.336.d:
पालयिष्ये प्रजाश्चेति पूर्वं ते समयः कृतः ..
तांस्तथावादिनः सर्वान्ब्रह्मर्षीनब्रवीत्तदा .. 81 ..
16.336.m: Formerly your covenant was made: “I will protect the subjects.”’ / To all those brahmin seers who spoke thus, (81)

16.336.s:
venaḥ prahasya durbuddhiridaṃ vacanakovidaḥ ..
sraṣṭā dharmasya kaścānyaḥ śrotavyaṃ kasya vā mayā .. 82 ..
16.336.d:
वेनः प्रहस्य दुर्बुद्धिरिदं वचनकोविदः ..
स्रष्टा धर्मस्य कश्चान्यः श्रोतव्यं कस्य वा मया .. 82 ..
16.336.m: the evil-minded Vena, skilled in words, laughed aloud and said: / ‘Who else is the creator of dharma, or whom else should I heed? (82)

16.336.s:
vīryaśrutatapaḥsatyairmayānyaḥ kaḥ samo bhuvi ..
madātmāno na nūnaṃ māṃ yūyaṃ jānītha tattvataḥ .. 83 ..
16.336.d:
वीर्यश्रुततपःसत्यैर्मयान्यः कः समो भुवि ..
मदात्मानो न नूनं मां यूयं जानीथ तत्त्वतः .. 83 ..
16.336.m: Who else on earth is equal to me in valour, sacred learning, austerity, and truth? / Thinking you are everything, you surely do not know me in reality! (83)

16.336.s:
prabhavaṃ sarvalokānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ..
itthaṃ dehena pṛthivīṃ bhāvena yajanena ca .. 84 ..
16.336.d:
प्रभवं सर्वलोकानां धर्माणां च विशेषतः..
इत्थं देहेन पृथिवीं भावेन यजनेन च .. 84 ..
16.336.m: The origin of all the worlds, and especially of dharmas— / thus with my body, my nature, and through sacrifice, (84)

16.336.s:
sṛjeyaṃ ca graseyaṃ ca nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
yadā na śakyate staṃbhānmattaścaiva vimohitaḥ .. 85 ..
16.336.d:
सृजेयं च ग्रसेयं च नात्र कार्या विचारणा ..
यदा न शक्यते स्तंभान्मत्तश्चैव विमोहितः .. 85 ..
16.336.m: I could create the earth and consume it; no doubt need be had in this matter.’ / When it was impossible to persuade King Vena, (85)

16.336.s:
anunetuṃ nṛpo venastatra kruddhā maharṣayaḥ ..
ātharvaṇena maṃtreṇa hatvā taṃ te mahābalam .. 86 ..
16.336.d:
अनुनेतुं नृपो वेनस्तत्र क्रुद्धा महर्षयः ..
आथर्वणेन मंत्रेण हत्वा तं ते महाबलम् .. 86 ..
16.336.m: who was arrogant through obstinacy and utterly infatuated, the great seers grew enraged; / having slain that mighty one with an Atharvan mantra, (86)

16.336.s:
tato'sya vāmabāhuṃ te mamaṃthurbhṛśakopitāḥ ..
tasmācca mathyamānādvai jajñe pūrvamiti śrutiḥ .. 87 ..
16.336.d:
ततोऽस्य वामबाहुं ते ममंथुर्भृशकोपिताः ..
तस्माच्च मथ्यमानाद्वै जज्ञे पूर्वमिति श्रुतिः .. 87 ..
16.336.m: they then churned his left arm in extreme fury. / And from that arm being churned, it is heard in tradition, there was born first (87)

16.336.s:
hrasvo'timātraḥ puruṣaḥ kṛṣṇaścāpi tadā priye ..
sa bhītaḥ prāñjaliścaiva tasthivānsaṃmukhe priye .. 88 ..
16.336.d:
ह्रस्वोऽतिमात्रः पुरुषः कृष्णश्चापि तदा प्रिये ..
स भीतः प्राञ्जलिश्चैव तस्थिवान्संमुखे प्रिये .. 88 ..
16.336.m: an exceedingly dwarfish man, black in colour, O beloved! / Terrified, with folded hands, he stood before them, O dear one. (88)

16.336.s:
tamāttaṃ vihvalaṃ dṛṣṭvā niṣīdetyabruvankila ..
niṣādo vaṃśakartā vai tenābhūtpṛthuvikramaḥ .. 89 ..
16.336.d:
तमात्तं विह्वलं दृष्ट्वा निषीदेत्यब्रुवन्किल ..
निषादो वंशकर्ता वै तेनाभूत्पृथुविक्रमः .. 89 ..
16.336.m: Seeing him distressed and overwhelmed, they said, ‘Sit down’ (niṣīda). / From him arose the Niṣāda of broad prowess, the founder of the lineage. (89)

16.336.s:
dhīvarānasṛjaccāpi venapāpasamudbhavān ..
ye cānye vindhyanilayāstathā vai tuṃbarāḥ khasāḥ .. 7.1.336.90 ..
16.336.d:
धीवरानसृजच्चापि वेनपापसमुद्भवान् ..
ये चान्ये विन्ध्यनिलयास्तथा वै तुंबराः खसाः .. 7.1.336.90 ..
16.336.m: He also produced the fishermen (dhīvara) who arose from the sin of Vena, / and those others who dwell in the Vindhya, as well as the Tumburas and Khasas. (90)

16.336.s:
adharme rucayaścāpi varddhitā venapāpajāḥ ..
punarmaharṣayastetha pāṇiṃ venasya dakṣiṇam ..91..
16.336.d:
अधर्मे रुचयश्चापि वर्द्धिता वेनपापजाः ..
पुनर्महर्षयस्तेथ पाणिं वेनस्य दक्षिणम् ..91..
16.336.m: Delighting in unrighteousness, these who sprang from Vena's sin multiplied. / Then the great seers, agitated and filled with wrath, (91)

16.336.s:
araṇīmiva saṃrabdhā mamaṃthurjāta manyavaḥ ..
pṛthustasmātsamutpannaḥ karājjvalanasaṃnibhaḥ .. 92 ..
16.336.d:
अरणीमिव संरब्धा ममंथुर्जात मन्यवः ..
पृथुस्तस्मात्समुत्पन्नः कराज्ज्वलनसंनिभः .. 92 ..
16.336.m: churned the right hand of Vena like a fire-drill. / From that hand arose Pṛthu, blazing like fire. (92)

16.336.s:
pṛthoḥ karatalāccāpi yasmājātastataḥ pṛthuḥ ..
dīpyamānaśca vapuṣā sākṣādagniriva jvalan .. 93 ..
16.336.d:
पृथोः करतलाच्चापि यस्माजातस्ततः पृथुः ..
दीप्यमानश्च वपुषा साक्षादग्निरिव ज्वलन् .. 93 ..
16.336.m: Because he was born from the broad (pṛthu) palm of the hand, he was therefore named Pṛthu; / he shone with his form like burning fire incarnate, (93)

16.336.s:
dhanurājagavaṃ gṛhya śarāṃścāśīviṣopamān ..
khaṅgaṃ ca rakṣanrakṣārthaṃ kavacaṃ ca mahāprabham .. 94 ..
16.336.d:
धनुराजगवं गृह्य शरांश्चाशीविषोपमान् ..
खङ्गं च रक्षन्रक्षार्थं कवचं च महाप्रभम् .. 94 ..
16.336.m: holding the Ajagava bow and arrows resembling venomous serpents, / carrying a sword for protection, and clad in radiant armour. (94)

16.336.s:
tasmiñjāte'tha bhūtāni saṃprahṛṣṭāni sarvaśaḥ ..
saṃbabhūvurmahādevi venaśca tridivaṃ gataḥ .. 95 ..
16.336.d:
तस्मिञ्जातेऽथ भूतानि संप्रहृष्टानि सर्वशः ..
संबभूवुर्महादेवि वेनश्च त्रिदिवं गतः .. 95 ..
16.336.m: When he was born, all beings rejoiced exceedingly on every side, / O great goddess, and Vena went to heaven. (95)

16.336.s:
tato nadyaḥ samudrāśca ratnānyādāya sarvaśaḥ ..
abhiṣekāya te sarve rājānamupatasthire .. .. 96 ..
16.336.d:
ततो नद्यः समुद्राश्च रत्नान्यादाय सर्वशः ..
अभिषेकाय ते सर्वे राजानमुपतस्थिरे .. .. 96 ..
16.336.m: Then the rivers and oceans, bringing jewels from all sides, / all attended upon the king for his consecration. (96)

16.336.s:
pitāmahaśca bhagavānṛṣibhiśca sahāmaraiḥ ..
sthāvarāṇi ca bhūtāni jaṃgamāni ca sarvaśaḥ .. 97 ..
16.336.d:
पितामहश्च भगवानृषिभिश्च सहामरैः ..
स्थावराणि च भूतानि जंगमानि च सर्वशः .. 97 ..
16.336.m: And the venerable Grandfather [Brahmā], together with the seers and immortals, / and all beings, both stationary and moving, from every quarter, (97)

16.336.s:
samāgamya tadā vainyamabhyaṣiṃcannarādhi pam ..
so'bhiṣikto mahātejā devairaṃgirasādibhiḥ .. 98 ..
16.336.d:
समागम्य तदा वैन्यमभ्यषिंचन्नराधि पम् ..
सोऽभिषिक्तो महातेजा देवैरंगिरसादिभिः .. 98 ..
16.336.m: assembled then and consecrated the son of Vena as ruler of men. / Consecrated by the gods, Aṅgiras and the others, (98)

16.336.s:
adhirājye mahābhāgaḥ pṛthurvainyaḥ pratāpavān ..
pitrā na raṃjitāścāsya prajā vainyena raṃjitāḥ .. 99 ..
16.336.d:
अधिराज्ये महाभागः पृथुर्वैन्यः प्रतापवान् ..
पित्रा न रंजिताश्चास्य प्रजा वैन्येन रंजिताः .. 99 ..
16.336.m: the illustrious and valorous Pṛthu, son of Vena, assumed supreme sovereignty. / The subjects who had not been gladdened by his father were gladdened by Vena's son. (99)

16.336.s:
tato rājeti nāmāsya anurāgādajāyata ..
āpaḥ stastaṃbhire cāsya samudramabhiyāsyataḥ .. 7.1.336.100 ..
16.336.d:
ततो राजेति नामास्य अनुरागादजायत ..
आपः स्तस्तंभिरे चास्य समुद्रमभियास्यतः .. 7.1.336.100 ..
16.336.m: Then his name became ‘king’ (rājan) from their affection (anurāga). / The waters became rigid as he marched towards the ocean; (100)

16.336.s:
parvatāścāpi śīryaṃte dhvajasaṃgo'pi nā'bhavat ..
akṛṣṭapacyā pṛthivī sidhyaṃtyannāni ciṃtayā ..
sarvakāmadughā gāvaḥ puṭakepuṭake madhu .. 101 ..
16.336.d:
पर्वताश्चापि शीर्यंते ध्वजसंगोऽपि नाऽभवत् ..
अकृष्टपच्या पृथिवी सिध्यंत्यन्नानि चिंतया ..
सर्वकामदुघा गावः पुटकेपुटके मधु .. 101 ..
16.336.m: the mountains crumbled, and his banner never met with obstruction. / The earth bore crops without ploughing; food was produced merely by thought; / cows yielded all desires; and honey was in every fold of leaf. (101)

16.336.s:
tasminneva tadā kāle puna rjajñe'tha māgadhaḥ ..
sāmageṣu ca gāyatsu srugbhāṃḍādvaiśvadevikāt .. 102 ..
16.336.d:
तस्मिन्नेव तदा काले पुन र्जज्ञेऽथ मागधः ..
सामगेषु च गायत्सु स्रुग्भांडाद्वैश्वदेविकात् .. 102 ..
16.336.m: At that very time, the Māgadha was also born, / from the vessel of the ladle used for all the gods, while the Sāman-singers were chanting. (102)

16.336.s:
sāmageṣu samutpannastasmānmagadha ucyate ..
aiṃdreṇa haviṣā cāpi haviḥ pṛktaṃ bṛhaspatiḥ .. 103 ..
16.336.d:
सामगेषु समुत्पन्नस्तस्मान्मगध उच्यते ..
ऐंद्रेण हविषा चापि हविः पृक्तं बृहस्पतिः .. 103 ..
16.336.m: Because he was born among the Sāman-singers (sāmageṣu), he is called a Magadha. / And the oblation was mixed with Indra's oblation when Bṛhaspati (103)

16.336.s:
yadā juhāva ceṃdrāya tatastato vyajāyata ..
pramādastatra saṃjajñe prāyaścittaṃ ca karmasu .. 104 ..
16.336.d:
यदा जुहाव चेंद्राय ततस्ततो व्यजायत ..
प्रमादस्तत्र संजज्ञे प्रायश्चित्तं च कर्मसु .. 104 ..
16.336.m: poured the sacrifice to Indra; from that [error] it was born. / An inadvertence occurred there, and an expiation in the rituals: (104)

16.336.s:
śeṣahavyena yatpṛktamabhibhūtaṃ gurorhaviḥ ..
adharottarasvāreṇa jajñe tadvarṇavaikṛtam ..105..
16.336.d:
शेषहव्येन यत्पृक्तमभिभूतं गुरोर्हविः ..
अधरोत्तरस्वारेण जज्ञे तद्वर्णवैकृतम् ..105..
16.336.m: because the oblation of the Guru [Bṛhaspati] was mixed with and overpowered by the remaining oblation, / through an inversion of high and low musical accents, that alteration of class was born. (105)

16.336.s:
yajñastasyāṃ samabhavadbrāhmaṇyāṃ kṣatrayonitaḥ ..
tataḥ pūrveṇa sādharmyāttulyadharmāḥ prakīrttitāḥ.. .. 106 ..
16.336.d:
यज्ञस्तस्यां समभवद्ब्राह्मण्यां क्षत्रयोनितः ..
ततः पूर्वेण साधर्म्यात्तुल्यधर्माः प्रकीर्त्तिताः.. .. 106 ..
16.336.m: A sacrificial origin arose in that brahmin woman from a kṣatriya source. / Therefore, because of resemblance in duty with the former, their duties are declared to be equal. (106)

16.336.s:
madhyamo hyeṣa tattvasya dharmaḥ kṣatropajīvanam ..
rathanāgāśvacaritaṃ jaghanyaṃ ca cikitsitam .. 107 ..
16.336.d:
मध्यमो ह्येष तत्त्वस्य धर्मः क्षत्रोपजीवनम् ..
रथनागाश्वचरितं जघन्यं च चिकित्सितम् .. 107 ..
16.336.m: For this middling duty in truth consists of living by the kṣatriya way— / the management of chariots, elephants, and horses, while the lowest [occupation] is medicine. (107)

16.336.s:
pṛthoḥ kathārthaṃ tau tatra samā hūtau maharṣibhiḥ ..
tāvūcurmunayaḥ sarve stūyatāmiti pārthivaḥ .. 108 ..
16.336.d:
पृथोः कथार्थं तौ तत्र समा हूतौ महर्षिभिः ..
तावूचुर्मुनयः सर्वे स्तूयतामिति पार्थिवः .. 108 ..
16.336.m: For the purpose of recounting [the deeds of] Pṛthu, the two were summoned there by the great seers. / All the sages said to them: 'Let the king be praised!

16.336.s:
karmabhiścānurūpo hi yatoyaṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ ..
tānūcatustadā sarvānṛṣīṃśca sūtamāgadhau .. 109 ..
16.336.d:
कर्मभिश्चानुरूपो हि यतोयं पृथिवीपतिः ..
तानूचतुस्तदा सर्वानृषींश्च सूतमागधौ .. 109 ..
16.336.m: For this ruler of the earth is indeed worthy because of his deeds.' / Then the bard and the herald said to all the seers:

16.336.s:
āvāṃ devānṛṣīṃścaiva prīṇayāva svakarmabhiḥ ..
na cāsya vidvo vai karma na tathā lakṣaṇaṃ yaśa .. 7.1.336.110 ..
16.336.d:
आवां देवानृषींश्चैव प्रीणयाव स्वकर्मभिः ..
न चास्य विद्वो वै कर्म न तथा लक्षणं यश .. 7.1.336.110 ..
16.336.m: 'We two please the gods and the seers through our own functions; / but we do not know his deeds, nor his characteristic glory,

16.336.s:
stotraṃ yenāsya saṃkurvo rājñastejasvino dvijāḥ ..
ṛṣibhistau niyuktau tu bhaviṣyaiḥ stūyatāmiti ..111..
16.336.d:
स्तोत्रं येनास्य संकुर्वो राज्ञस्तेजस्विनो द्विजाः ..
ऋषिभिस्तौ नियुक्तौ तु भविष्यैः स्तूयतामिति ..111..
16.336.m: by which we may compose a hymn of praise for this glorious king, O twice-born ones.' / But those two were instructed by the seers: 'Let him be praised by [the deeds] yet to come!'

16.336.s:
yāni karmāṇi kṛtavānpṛthuḥ paścānmahābalaḥ ..
tāni gītāni baddhāni stuvadbhiḥ sūtamāgadhaiḥ .. 112 ..
tataḥ śrutārthaḥ suprītaḥ pṛthuḥ prādātprajeśvaraḥ ..
anūpadeśaṃ sūtāya māgadhānmāgadhāya ca .. 1 13..
16.336.d:
यानि कर्माणि कृतवान्पृथुः पश्चान्महाबलः ..
तानि गीतानि बद्धानि स्तुवद्भिः सूतमागधैः .. 112 ..
ततः श्रुतार्थः सुप्रीतः पृथुः प्रादात्प्रजेश्वरः ..
अनूपदेशं सूताय मागधान्मागधाय च .. 1 13..
16.336.m:
The deeds which the mighty Pṛthu performed afterwards, / those were sung and composed by the praising bards and heralds.
Then the lord of subjects, Pṛthu, pleased with what he heard, / granted the Anūpa country to the bard, and the Magadha regions to the herald.

16.336.s:
tadādi pṛthivīpālāḥ stūyante sūtamāgadhaiḥ ..
āśīrvādaiḥ praśaṃsyaṃte sūtamāgadhabaṃdibhiḥ .. 114 ..
16.336.d:
तदादि पृथिवीपालाः स्तूयन्ते सूतमागधैः ..
आशीर्वादैः प्रशंस्यंते सूतमागधबंदिभिः .. 114 ..
16.336.m: From then on, earthly rulers are praised by bards and heralds; / they are extolled with benedictions by bards, heralds, and panegyrists.

16.336.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā paramaṃ prītāḥ prajā ūcurmaharṣayaḥ ..
eṣa vo vṛttido vainyo vihito'tha narādhipaḥ .. 115 ..
16.336.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा परमं प्रीताः प्रजा ऊचुर्महर्षयः ..
एष वो वृत्तिदो वैन्यो विहितोऽथ नराधिपः .. 115 ..
16.336.m: Seeing him, the great seers, exceedingly delighted, said to the subjects: / 'This son of Vena has now been appointed your king, the provider of your livelihood.'

16.336.s:
tato vainyaṃ mahābhāgaṃ prajāḥ samabhidudruvuḥ ..
tvaṃ no vṛttividhāteti maharṣivacanāttathā .. .. 116 ..
16.336.d:
ततो वैन्यं महाभागं प्रजाः समभिदुद्रुवुः ..
त्वं नो वृत्तिविधातेति महर्षिवचनात्तथा .. .. 116 ..
16.336.m: Then the subjects ran up to the illustrious son of Vena, / saying, 'You are the dispenser of our livelihood,' according to the words of the great seers.

16.336.s:
so'bhīhitaḥ prajābhistu prajāhitacikīrṣayā ..
dhanurgṛhītvā bāṇāṃśca vasudhāmārdayadbalī .. 117 ..
16.336.d:
सोऽभीहितः प्रजाभिस्तु प्रजाहितचिकीर्षया ..
धनुर्गृहीत्वा बाणांश्च वसुधामार्दयद्बली .. 117 ..
16.336.m: Thus addressed by the subjects, and wishing to do good for the subjects, / the mighty one took up his bow and arrows and assailed the earth.

16.336.s:
tato vainyabhayatrastā gaurbhūtvā prādravanmahī ..
tāṃ dhenuṃ pṛthurādāya dravantīmanvadhāvata .. 118 ..
16.336.d:
ततो वैन्यभयत्रस्ता गौर्भूत्वा प्राद्रवन्मही ..
तां धेनुं पृथुरादाय द्रवन्तीमन्वधावत .. 118 ..
16.336.m: Then the earth, terrified by fear of the son of Vena, turned into a cow and fled. / Taking up [his weapon], Pṛthu pursued that fleeing cow.

16.336.s:
sā lokānbrahmalokādīngatvā vainyabhayāttadā ..
dadarśa cāgrato vainyaṃ kārmukodyatapāṇinam .. 119 ..
16.336.d:
सा लोकान्ब्रह्मलोकादीन्गत्वा वैन्यभयात्तदा ..
ददर्श चाग्रतो वैन्यं कार्मुकोद्यतपाणिनम् .. 119 ..
16.336.m: Having gone through the worlds beginning with the world of Brahmā out of fear of the son of Vena, / she saw the son of Vena in front of her, his hand raising the bow,

16.336.s:
jvaladbhirviśikhaistīkṣṇairdīptatejaḥsamanvitaiḥ ..
mahāyogaṃ mahātmānaṃ durddharṣamamarairapi .. 7.1.336.120 ..
16.336.d:
ज्वलद्भिर्विशिखैस्तीक्ष्णैर्दीप्ततेजःसमन्वितैः ..
महायोगं महात्मानं दुर्द्धर्षममरैरपि .. 7.1.336.120 ..
16.336.m: with sharp, blazing arrows endowed with burning splendour— / him of great yoga, the great-souled one, unassailable even by the immortals.

16.336.s:
alabhaṃtī tu sā trāṇaṃ vainyamevābhyapadyata ..
kṛtāṃjalipuṭā devī pūjyā lokaistribhissadā ..121..
16.336.d:
अलभंती तु सा त्राणं वैन्यमेवाभ्यपद्यत ..
कृतांजलिपुटा देवी पूज्या लोकैस्त्रिभिस्सदा ..121..
16.336.m: Finding no protection, she surrendered to the son of Vena alone, / with her hands folded in reverence—the goddess who is ever worthy of worship by the three worlds.

16.336.s:
uvāca cainaṃ nādharmyaṃ strīvadhaṃ paripaśyasi ..
kathaṃ dhārayitā cāsi prajā rājanmayā vinā .. 122 ..
16.336.d:
उवाच चैनं नाधर्म्यं स्त्रीवधं परिपश्यसि ..
कथं धारयिता चासि प्रजा राजन्मया विना .. 122 ..
16.336.m: And she said to him: 'Do you not see the slaughter of a woman to be unrighteous? / And how will you sustain the subjects, O king, without me?

16.336.s:
mayi lokāḥ sthitā rājanmayedaṃ dhāryate jagat ..
madṛte tu vinaśyeyuḥ prajāḥ pārthiva viddhi tat .. 123 ..
16.336.d:
मयि लोकाः स्थिता राजन्मयेदं धार्यते जगत् ..
मदृते तु विनश्येयुः प्रजाः पार्थिव विद्धि तत् .. 123 ..
16.336.m: Upon me the worlds rest, O king; by me this universe is upheld. / Know that without me the subjects would perish, O ruler of the earth.

16.336.s:
sa māṃ nārhasi haṃtuṃ vai śreyaścettvaṃ cikīrṣasi ..
prajānāṃ pṛthivīpāla śṛṇuṣvedaṃ vaco mama ..124..
16.336.d:
स मां नार्हसि हंतुं वै श्रेयश्चेत्त्वं चिकीर्षसि ..
प्रजानां पृथिवीपाल शृणुष्वेदं वचो मम ..124..
16.336.m: Therefore you ought not to kill me, if you wish to bring about the welfare / of the subjects, O guardian of the earth! Listen to these words of mine:

16.336.s:
upāyataḥ samārabdhāḥ sarve sidhyaṃtyupakramāḥ ..
hatvā māṃ tvaṃ na śakto vai prajāḥ pālayituṃ nṛpa .. 125 ..
16.336.d:
उपायतः समारब्धाः सर्वे सिध्यंत्युपक्रमाः ..
हत्वा मां त्वं न शक्तो वै प्रजाः पालयितुं नृप .. 125 ..
16.336.m: All undertakings begun with the proper means succeed. / Having killed me, you will certainly not be able to protect the subjects, O king.

16.336.s:
anukūlā bhaviṣyāmi tyaja kopaṃ mahādyute ..
avadhyāśca striyaḥ prāhustiryagyonigatā api .. ..126..
16.336.d:
अनुकूला भविष्यामि त्यज कोपं महाद्युते ..
अवध्याश्च स्त्रियः प्राहुस्तिर्यग्योनिगता अपि .. ..126..
16.336.m: I shall be compliant; cast off your anger, O one of great splendour! / They say that females are not to be slain, even those born as animals.

16.336.s:
ekasminnidhanaṃ prāpte pāpiṣṭhe krūrakarmaṇi ..
bahūnāṃ bhavati kṣemastatra puṇyaprado vadhaḥ ..
satyevaṃ pṛthivīpāla dharmmaṃ mā tyaktumarhasi ..127..
16.336.d:
एकस्मिन्निधनं प्राप्ते पापिष्ठे क्रूरकर्मणि ..
बहूनां भवति क्षेमस्तत्र पुण्यप्रदो वधः ..
सत्येवं पृथिवीपाल धर्म्मं मा त्यक्तुमर्हसि ..127..
16.336.m: When destruction befalls a single, most sinful person of cruel deeds, / safety arises for many; in that case killing confers merit. / Though this is so, O protector of the earth, you should not abandon righteousness.'

16.336.s:
evaṃvidhaṃ tu tadvākyaṃ śrutvā rājā mahābalaḥ ..
krodhaṃ nigṛhya dharmātmā vasudhāmidamabravīt .. 128 ..
16.336.d:
एवंविधं तु तद्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा राजा महाबलः ..
क्रोधं निगृह्य धर्मात्मा वसुधामिदमब्रवीत् .. 128 ..
16.336.m: Hearing such speech of hers, the mighty king, / restraining his anger, the righteous one spoke thus to the earth:

16.336.s:
ekasyārthe ca yo hanyādātmano vā parasya vā ..
ekaṃ vāpi bahūnvāpi kāmataścāsti pātakam .. 129 ..
16.336.d:
एकस्यार्थे च यो हन्यादात्मनो वा परस्य वा ..
एकं वापि बहून्वापि कामतश्चास्ति पातकम् .. 129 ..
16.336.m: 'Whoever would kill one or even many, wilfully, / for the sake of one person—whether oneself or another—incurs a sin.

16.336.s:
yasmiṃstu nidhanaṃ prāptā edhante bahavaḥ sukham ..
tasminhate ca bhūyo hi pātakaṃ nāsti tasya vai .. 7.1.336.130 ..
16.336.d:
यस्मिंस्तु निधनं प्राप्ता एधन्ते बहवः सुखम् ..
तस्मिन्हते च भूयो हि पातकं नास्ति तस्य वै .. 7.1.336.130 ..
16.336.m: When one is destroyed, however, and many thrive in happiness, / there is indeed no further sin for him when that one is slain.

16.336.s:
so'haṃ prajānimittaṃ tvāṃ haniṣyāmi vasundhare ..
yadi me vacanaṃ nādya kariṣyasi jagaddhitam .. 131 ..
16.336.d:
सोऽहं प्रजानिमित्तं त्वां हनिष्यामि वसुन्धरे ..
यदि मे वचनं नाद्य करिष्यसि जगद्धितम् .. 131 ..
16.336.m: Therefore, for the sake of the subjects, I shall kill you, O bearer of wealth, / if you will not do my bidding today for the welfare of the world.

16.336.s:
tvāṃ nihatyādya bāṇena macchāsanaparāṅmukhīm..
ātmānaṃ pṛthukṛtveha prajā dhārayitāsmyaham ..132..
16.336.d:
त्वां निहत्याद्य बाणेन मच्छासनपराङ्मुखीम्..
आत्मानं पृथुकृत्वेह प्रजा धारयितास्म्यहम् ..132..
16.336.m: Having slain you today with an arrow, averse as you are to my command, / I myself shall make myself vast and uphold the subjects here.

16.336.s:
sā tvaṃ vacanamāsthāya mama dharmabhṛtāṃvare..
sañjīvaya prajā nityaṃ śaktā hyasi na saṃśayaḥ .. 133 ..
16.336.d:
सा त्वं वचनमास्थाय मम धर्मभृतांवरे..
सञ्जीवय प्रजा नित्यं शक्ता ह्यसि न संशयः .. 133 ..
16.336.m: So, relying on my word, O best among upholders of righteousness, / keep the subjects alive constantly, for you are indeed capable, there is no doubt.

16.336.s:
duhitṛtvaṃ hi me gaccha evametanmahaccharam ..
niyacche tvadvadhārthaṃ ca prayuktaṃ ghoradarśanam ..
pratyuvāca tato vainyamevamuktā mahāsatī .. 134 ..
16.336.d:
दुहितृत्वं हि मे गच्छ एवमेतन्महच्छरम् ..
नियच्छे त्वद्वधार्थं च प्रयुक्तं घोरदर्शनम् ..
प्रत्युवाच ततो वैन्यमेवमुक्ता महासती .. 134 ..
16.336.m: Become my daughter, and thus I shall withdraw this great arrow, / terrible to behold, which has been deployed to kill you.' / Thus addressed, the greatly chaste [earth] then replied to the son of Vena:

16.336.s:
sarvametadahaṃ rājanvidhāsyāmi na saṃśayaḥ ..
vatsaṃ tu mama saṃyukṣva kṣareyaṃ yena vatsalā .. 135 ..
16.336.d:
सर्वमेतदहं राजन्विधास्यामि न संशयः ..
वत्सं तु मम संयुक्ष्व क्षरेयं येन वत्सला .. 135 ..
16.336.m: 'I shall arrange all this, O king, there is no doubt. / But provide a calf for me, by which I, full of affection, may yield milk.

16.336.s:
samāṃ ca kuru sarvatra māṃ tvaṃ sarvabhṛtāṃ vara ..
yathā visyandamānāhaṃ kṣīraṃ sarvatra bhāvaye ..136..
16.336.d:
समां च कुरु सर्वत्र मां त्वं सर्वभृतां वर ..
यथा विस्यन्दमानाहं क्षीरं सर्वत्र भावये ..136..
16.336.m: And make me level everywhere, O best of all beings, / so that, flowing forth, I may cause the milk to spread everywhere.'

16.336.s:
.. īśvara uvāca .. ..
tata utsārayāmāsa śilājālāni sarvaśaḥ..
dhanuṣkoṭyā tato vainyastena śailā vivarddhitāḥ ..137..
16.336.d:
.. ईश्वर उवाच .. ..
तत उत्सारयामास शिलाजालानि सर्वशः..
धनुष्कोट्या ततो वैन्यस्तेन शैला विवर्द्धिताः ..137..
16.336.m: Īśvara said: / Then the son of Vena cleared away masses of rocks everywhere / with the tip of his bow; thereby the mountains were elevated.

16.336.s:
manvatareṣvatīteṣu caivamāsīdvasundharā ..
svabhāvenābhavattasyāḥ samāni viṣamāṇi ca ..138..
16.336.d:
मन्वतरेष्वतीतेषु चैवमासीद्वसुन्धरा ..
स्वभावेनाभवत्तस्याः समानि विषमाणि च ..138..
16.336.m: In past manvantaras the earth was indeed like this; / by her natural state she had level and uneven [surfaces].

16.336.s:
na hi pūrvanisarge vai viṣamaṃ pṛthivītalam..
pravibhāgaḥ purāṇāṃ ca grāmāṇāṃ cātha vidyate .. 139 ..
16.336.d:
न हि पूर्वनिसर्गे वै विषमं पृथिवीतलम्..
प्रविभागः पुराणां च ग्रामाणां चाथ विद्यते .. 139 ..
16.336.m: For in the previous creation the earth's surface was not uneven, / nor did there exist any division into cities and villages,

16.336.s: na sasyāni na gorakṣaṃ na kṛṣirna vaṇikpathaḥ .. 7.1.336.140 ..
16.336.d: न सस्यानि न गोरक्षं न कृषिर्न वणिक्पथः .. 7.1.336.140 ..
16.336.m: nor crops, nor cattle-herding, nor agriculture, nor trade routes.

16.336.s:
cākṣuṣasyāṃtare pūrvamāsīdetatpurā kila ..
vaivasvate'ntare cāsminsarvasyaitasya saṃbhavaḥ ..
samatvaṃ yatrayatrāsīdbhūmeḥ kasmiṃścideva hi..141..
16.336.d:
चाक्षुषस्यांतरे पूर्वमासीदेतत्पुरा किल ..
वैवस्वतेऽन्तरे चास्मिन्सर्वस्यैतस्य संभवः ..
समत्वं यत्रयत्रासीद्भूमेः कस्मिंश्चिदेव हि..141..
16.336.m: Formerly, in the interval of Cākṣuṣa [Manu], this was so in the past; / but in this interval of Vaivasvata the origin of all this took place. / Wherever in some places there was levelness of the earth,

16.336.s:
tatratatra prajāstā vai nivasanti sma sarvadā ..
āhāraḥ phalamūlaṃ tu prajānāmabhavatkila .. 142 ..
16.336.d:
तत्रतत्र प्रजास्ता वै निवसन्ति स्म सर्वदा ..
आहारः फलमूलं तु प्रजानामभवत्किल .. 142 ..
16.336.m: there those subjects always dwelt. / The food of the subjects was indeed fruits and roots,

16.336.s:
kṛcchreṇaiva tadā tāsāmityevamanuśuśruma ..
vainyātprabhṛtiloke'sminsarvasyaitasya saṃbhavaḥ ..143..
16.336.d:
कृच्छ्रेणैव तदा तासामित्येवमनुशुश्रुम ..
वैन्यात्प्रभृतिलोकेऽस्मिन्सर्वस्यैतस्य संभवः ..143..
16.336.m: obtained with difficulty by them at that time—thus indeed have we heard. / Beginning with the son of Vena, the origin of all this occurred in this world.

16.336.s:
saṃkalpayitvā vatsaṃ tu cākṣuṣaṃ manumīśvaram ..
pṛthurdudoha sasyāni svahaste pṛthivīṃ tataḥ ..144..
16.336.d:
संकल्पयित्वा वत्सं तु चाक्षुषं मनुमीश्वरम् ..
पृथुर्दुदोह सस्यानि स्वहस्ते पृथिवीं ततः ..144..
16.336.m: Having appointed the powerful Manu Cākṣuṣa as the calf, / Pṛthu then milked the crops from the earth with his own hand.

16.336.s:
sasyāni tena dugdhā vai venyeneyaṃ vasundharā ..
manuṃ vai cākṣuṣaṃ kṛtvā vatsaṃ pātre ca bhūmaye .. 145 ..
16.336.d:
सस्यानि तेन दुग्धा वै वेन्येनेयं वसुन्धरा ..
मनुं वै चाक्षुषं कृत्वा वत्सं पात्रे च भूमये .. 145 ..
16.336.m: Crops were thus milked from this earth by the son of Vena, / having made Manu Cākṣuṣa the calf, into an earthen vessel.

16.336.s:
tenānnena tadā tā vai varttayante sadā prajāḥ ..
ṛṣibhiḥ śrūyate cāpi punardugdhā vasundharā ..146..
16.336.d:
तेनान्नेन तदा ता वै वर्त्तयन्ते सदा प्रजाः ..
ऋषिभिः श्रूयते चापि पुनर्दुग्धा वसुन्धरा ..146..
16.336.m: Upon that food the subjects then always sustained themselves. / And it is heard that the earth was milked again by the seers.

16.336.s:
vatsaḥ somastatasteṣāṃ dogdhā cāpi bṛhaspatiḥ ..
pātramāsanhi cchandāṃsi gāyatryādīni sarvaśaḥ .. 147 ..
16.336.d:
वत्सः सोमस्ततस्तेषां दोग्धा चापि बृहस्पतिः ..
पात्रमासन्हि च्छन्दांसि गायत्र्यादीनि सर्वशः .. 147 ..
16.336.m: Then their calf was Soma, and the milker was Bṛhaspati; / the vessels were the metres, Gāyatrī and the rest, in every respect.

16.336.s:
kṣīramāsīttadā teṣāṃ tapo brahma ca śāśvatam..
punastato devagaṇaiḥ puraṃdarapurogamaiḥ .. 148 ..
16.336.d:
क्षीरमासीत्तदा तेषां तपो ब्रह्म च शाश्वतम्..
पुनस्ततो देवगणैः पुरंदरपुरोगमैः .. 148 ..
16.336.m: Their milk then was austerity and eternal sacred lore. / Then again by the hosts of gods, led by Puraṃdara,

16.336.s:
sauvarṇaṃ pātramādāya dugdheyaṃ śrūyate mahī ..
vatsastu maghavā cāsīddogdhā ca savitā'bhavat .. 149 ..
16.336.d:
सौवर्णं पात्रमादाय दुग्धेयं श्रूयते मही ..
वत्सस्तु मघवा चासीद्दोग्धा च सविताऽभवत् .. 149 ..
16.336.m: this earth is heard to have been milked, taking a golden vessel; / the calf was Maghavat, and Savitṛ became the milker.

16.336.s:
kṣīramūrjāmadhu proktaṃ vartaṃte tena devatāḥ ..
pitṛbhiḥ śrūyate cāpi punardugdhā vasundharā .. .. 7.1.336.150 ..
16.336.d:
क्षीरमूर्जामधु प्रोक्तं वर्तंते तेन देवताः ..
पितृभिः श्रूयते चापि पुनर्दुग्धा वसुन्धरा .. .. 7.1.336.150 ..
16.336.m: The milk was declared to be strength and nectar; by it the gods subsist. / And it is heard that the earth was milked again by the ancestors:

16.336.s:
rājataṃ pātramādāya svadhā tvakṣayyatṛptaye ..
vaivasvato yamastvāsītteṣāṃ vatsaḥ pratāpavān .. 151 ..
16.336.d:
राजतं पात्रमादाय स्वधा त्वक्षय्यतृप्तये ..
वैवस्वतो यमस्त्वासीत्तेषां वत्सः प्रतापवान् .. 151 ..
16.336.m: taking a silver vessel, [they milked] svadhā for imperishable satisfaction. / Yama, the son of Vivasvat, was their glorious calf;

16.336.s:
aṃtakaścābhavaddogdhā pitṛṇāṃ bhagavā nprabhuḥ ..
asuraiḥ śrūyate cāpi punardugdhā vasundharā .. 152 ..
16.336.d:
अंतकश्चाभवद्दोग्धा पितृणां भगवा न्प्रभुः ..
असुरैः श्रूयते चापि पुनर्दुग्धा वसुन्धरा .. 152 ..
16.336.m: and the lord, venerable Antaka, was the milker of the ancestors. / And it is heard that the earth was milked again by the asuras:

16.336.s:
āyasaṃ pātramādāya balamādhāya sarvaśaḥ ..
virocanastu prāhlādisteṣāṃ vatsaḥ pratāpavān .. 153 ..
16.336.d:
आयसं पात्रमादाय बलमाधाय सर्वशः ..
विरोचनस्तु प्राह्लादिस्तेषां वत्सः प्रतापवान् .. 153 ..
16.336.m: taking an iron vessel, gathering strength on every side, / Virocana, son of Prahlāda, was their glorious calf;

16.336.s:
ṛtvigdvimūrddhā daityānāṃ dogdhā tu ditinandanaḥ ..
māyākṣīraṃ dudohāsau daityānāṃ tṛptikārakam .. 154 ..
16.336.d:
ऋत्विग्द्विमूर्द्धा दैत्यानां दोग्धा तु दितिनन्दनः ..
मायाक्षीरं दुदोहासौ दैत्यानां तृप्तिकारकम् .. 154 ..
16.336.m: the priest Dvimūrdhan, son of Diti, was the milker of the daityas. / He milked the milk of illusion, which brought satisfaction to the daityas.

16.336.s:
tenaite māyayā'dyāpi sarve māyāvido'surāḥ ..
varttayaṃti mahāvīryāstadeteṣāṃ paraṃ balam.. 155 ..
16.336.d:
तेनैते माययाऽद्यापि सर्वे मायाविदोऽसुराः ..
वर्त्तयंति महावीर्यास्तदेतेषां परं बलम्.. 155 ..
16.336.m: Through that illusion even today all those asuras, knowers of illusion, / subsist, possessing great power; for that is their supreme strength.

16.336.s:
nāgaiśca śrūyate dugdhā vatsaṃ kṛtvā tu takṣakam ..
alābupātramādāya viṣaṃ kṣīraṃ tadā mahat .. 156 ..
16.336.d:
नागैश्च श्रूयते दुग्धा वत्सं कृत्वा तु तक्षकम् ..
अलाबुपात्रमादाय विषं क्षीरं तदा महत् .. 156 ..
16.336.m: And it is heard that [the earth] was milked by the nāgas, making Takṣaka the calf; / taking a gourd vessel, [they milked] great poison as their milk then.

16.336.s:
teṣāṃ vai vāsukirdogdhā kādraveyo mahāyaśāḥ ..
nāgānāṃ vai mahādevi sarpāṇāṃ caiva sarvaśaḥ ..157..
16.336.d:
तेषां वै वासुकिर्दोग्धा काद्रवेयो महायशाः ..
नागानां वै महादेवि सर्पाणां चैव सर्वशः ..157..
16.336.m: Vāsuki, the son of Kadrū of great renown, was their milker, / indeed of all the nāgas and serpents, O great goddess.

16.336.s:
tena vai varttayantyugrā mahākāyā viṣolbaṇāḥ ..
tadāhārāstadācārāstadvīryāstadapāśrayāḥ .. 158 ..
16.336.d:
तेन वै वर्त्तयन्त्युग्रा महाकाया विषोल्बणाः ..
तदाहारास्तदाचारास्तद्वीर्यास्तदपाश्रयाः .. 158 ..
16.336.m: By it they subsist, fierce, having huge bodies, swollen with poison, / having that for their food, conduct, strength, and refuge.

16.336.s:
āmapātre punardugdhā tvaṃtarddhānamiyaṃ mahī ..
vatsaṃ vaiśravaṇaṃ kṛtvā yakṣapuṇyajanaistathā .. 159 ..
16.336.d:
आमपात्रे पुनर्दुग्धा त्वंतर्द्धानमियं मही ..
वत्सं वैश्रवणं कृत्वा यक्षपुण्यजनैस्तथा .. 159 ..
16.336.m: Again, this earth was milked into an unbaked clay vessel for invisibility, / making Vaiśravaṇa the calf, by the yakṣas and puṇyajanas.

16.336.s:
dogdhā rajatanāgastu cintāmaṇicarastu yaḥ ..
yakṣādhipo mahātejā vaśī jñānī mahātapāḥ .. 7.1.336.160 ..
16.336.d:
दोग्धा रजतनागस्तु चिन्तामणिचरस्तु यः ..
यक्षाधिपो महातेजा वशी ज्ञानी महातपाः .. 7.1.336.160 ..
16.336.m: The milker was the silver serpent who moves about the Cintāmaṇi stone, / the lord of the yakṣas, endowed with great splendor, self-controlled, wise, and of great austerity.

16.336.s:
tena te varttayaṃ tīti yakṣā vasubhirūrjitaiḥ ..
rākṣasaiśca piśācaiśca punardugdhā vasundharā .. 161 ..
16.336.d:
तेन ते वर्त्तयं तीति यक्षा वसुभिरूर्जितैः ..
राक्षसैश्च पिशाचैश्च पुनर्दुग्धा वसुन्धरा .. 161 ..
16.336.m: By that they subsist, the yakṣas, with abundant riches. / And the earth was milked again by the rākṣasas and piśācas:

16.336.s:
brahmopendrastu dogdhā vai teṣāmāsītkuberataḥ ..
vatsaḥ sumālī balavānkṣīraṃ rudhirameva ca ..162..
16.336.d:
ब्रह्मोपेन्द्रस्तु दोग्धा वै तेषामासीत्कुबेरतः ..
वत्सः सुमाली बलवान्क्षीरं रुधिरमेव च ..162..
16.336.m: Brahmopendra was their milker from Kubera; / their calf was mighty Sumālin, and their milk was blood itself.

16.336.s:
kapālapātre nirdugdhā tvaṃtarddhānaṃ tu rākṣasaiḥ ..
tena kṣīreṇa rakṣāṃsi varttayantīha sarvaśaḥ ..163..
16.336.d:
कपालपात्रे निर्दुग्धा त्वंतर्द्धानं तु राक्षसैः ..
तेन क्षीरेण रक्षांसि वर्त्तयन्तीह सर्वशः ..163..
16.336.m: [She was] milked into a skull-vessel for invisibility by the rākṣasas. / By that milk the demons subsist here in every way.

16.336.s:
padmapatreṣu vai dugdhā gaṃdharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ ..
vatsaṃ caitrarathaṃ kṛtvā śucigandhānmahī tadā .. 164 ..
16.336.d:
पद्मपत्रेषु वै दुग्धा गंधर्वाप्सरसां गणैः ..
वत्सं चैत्ररथं कृत्वा शुचिगन्धान्मही तदा .. 164 ..
16.336.m: She was milked onto lotus leaves by the hosts of gandharvas and apsarases; / having made Citraratha the calf, [they milked] pure fragrances from the earth then.

16.336.s:
teṣāṃ vatso rucistvāsīddogdhā putro muneḥ śubhaḥ ..
śailaistu śrūyate devi punardugdhā vasuṃdharā .. 165 ..
16.336.d:
तेषां वत्सो रुचिस्त्वासीद्दोग्धा पुत्रो मुनेः शुभः ..
शैलैस्तु श्रूयते देवि पुनर्दुग्धा वसुंधरा .. 165 ..
16.336.m: Their calf was Ruci, and the virtuous son of the sage was the milker. / And it is heard, O goddess, that the earth was milked again by the mountains:

16.336.s:
tadauṣadhīrmūrtimatī ratnāni vividhāni ca ..
vatsastu himavāṃsteṣāṃ dogdhā merurmahāgiriḥ .. 166 ..
16.336.d:
तदौषधीर्मूर्तिमती रत्नानि विविधानि च ..
वत्सस्तु हिमवांस्तेषां दोग्धा मेरुर्महागिरिः .. 166 ..
16.336.m: then [they milked] embodied medicinal plants and various kinds of gems. / Himavat was their calf, and Mount Meru was the milker;

16.336.s:
pātraṃ śilāmayaṃ hyāsīttena śailāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ ..
śrūyate vṛkṣavīrudbhiḥ punardugdhā vasundharā .. 167 ..
16.336.d:
पात्रं शिलामयं ह्यासीत्तेन शैलाः प्रतिष्ठिताः ..
श्रूयते वृक्षवीरुद्भिः पुनर्दुग्धा वसुन्धरा .. 167 ..
16.336.m: the vessel was indeed made of stone, and by that the mountains were established. / It is heard that the earth was milked again by trees and creepers:

16.336.s:
pālāśaṃ pātramādāya cchinnadagdhaprarohaṇam ..
dogdhā tu puṣpitaḥ śālaḥ plakṣo vatso yaśasvini ..
sarvakāmadughā dogdhā pṛthivī bhūtabhāvinī .. 168 ..
16.336.d:
पालाशं पात्रमादाय च्छिन्नदग्धप्ररोहणम् ..
दोग्धा तु पुष्पितः शालः प्लक्षो वत्सो यशस्विनि ..
सर्वकामदुघा दोग्धा पृथिवी भूतभाविनी .. 168 ..
16.336.m: taking a vessel of palāśa wood, [they milked] sprouting when cut and burnt. / The flowering śāla tree was the milker, and the plakṣa was the calf, O illustrious one. / The earth, source of living beings, was milked yielding all desires.

16.336.s:
saiṣā dhātrī vidhātrī ca dharaṇī ca vasundharā ..
dugdhā hitārthaṃ lokānāṃ pṛthunā iti naḥ śrutam .. 169 ..
16.336.d:
सैषा धात्री विधात्री च धरणी च वसुन्धरा ..
दुग्धा हितार्थं लोकानां पृथुना इति नः श्रुतम् .. 169 ..
16.336.m: This very [earth], the nurse, the creator, the upholder, and the bearer of wealth, / was milked for the welfare of the worlds by Pṛthu, so we have heard.

16.336.s:
carācarasya lokasya pratiṣṭhā yonireva ca ..
āsīdiyaṃ samudrāṃtā medinīti pariśrutā..7.1.336.170..
16.336.d:
चराचरस्य लोकस्य प्रतिष्ठा योनिरेव च ..
आसीदियं समुद्रांता मेदिनीति परिश्रुता..7.1.336.170..
16.336.m: The support and the womb of the moving and unmoving world, / bounded by the ocean, she was celebrated as Medinī,

16.336.s:
madhukaiṭabhayoḥ pūrvaṃ medomāṃsapariplutā ..
vasundhārayate yasmādvasudhā tena kīrtitā .. 171 ..
16.336.d:
मधुकैटभयोः पूर्वं मेदोमांसपरिप्लुता ..
वसुन्धारयते यस्माद्वसुधा तेन कीर्तिता .. 171 ..
16.336.m: because she was formerly covered with the fat and flesh of Madhu and Kaiṭabha; / and since she holds wealth, for that reason she is celebrated as Vasudhā.

16.336.s:
tato'bhyupagamādrājñaḥ pṛthorvainyasya dhīmataḥ ..
duhitṛtvamanuprāptā pṛthivītyucyate tataḥ .. 172 ..
16.336.d:
ततोऽभ्युपगमाद्राज्ञः पृथोर्वैन्यस्य धीमतः ..
दुहितृत्वमनुप्राप्ता पृथिवीत्युच्यते ततः .. 172 ..
16.336.m: Then, through the acceptance of King Pṛthu, son of Vena, the wise, / she attained daughterhood, and hence she is called Pṛthivī.

16.336.s:
prathitā pravibhaktā ca śobhitā ca vasundharā ..
dugdhā hi yatnato rājñā pattanākaramālinī .. 173 ..
16.336.d:
प्रथिता प्रविभक्ता च शोभिता च वसुन्धरा ..
दुग्धा हि यत्नतो राज्ञा पत्तनाकरमालिनी .. 173 ..
16.336.m: Extended, divided, adorned, / and garlanded with cities and mines, the earth was diligently milked by the king.

16.336.s:
evaṃ prabhāvo rājāsīdvainyaḥ sa nṛpasattamaḥ ..
tataḥ sa raṃjayāmāsa dharmeṇa pṛthivīṃ tadā .. 174 ..
16.336.d:
एवं प्रभावो राजासीद्वैन्यः स नृपसत्तमः ..
ततः स रंजयामास धर्मेण पृथिवीं तदा .. 174 ..
16.336.m: Such was the majesty of that king, the son of Vena, best of kings. / Then he pleased the earth with righteousness at that time;

16.336.s:
tato rājeti śabdo'tha pṛthivyāṃ raṃjanādabhūt ..
sa rājyaṃ prāpya vainyastu ciṃtayāmāsa pārthivaḥ .. 175 ..
16.336.d:
ततो राजेति शब्दोऽथ पृथिव्यां रंजनादभूत् ..
स राज्यं प्राप्य वैन्यस्तु चिंतयामास पार्थिवः .. 175 ..
16.336.m: and so the title 'king' arose upon the earth from pleasing. / Having attained the kingdom, that king, the son of Vena, thought:

16.336.s:
pitā mama hyadharmiṣṭho yajñādyucchittikārakaḥ..
kasminsthāne gataścāsau jñeyaṃ sthānaṃ kathaṃ mayā .. 176 ..
16.336.d:
पिता मम ह्यधर्मिष्ठो यज्ञाद्युच्छित्तिकारकः..
कस्मिन्स्थाने गतश्चासौ ज्ञेयं स्थानं कथं मया .. 176 ..
16.336.m: “My father was indeed exceedingly unrighteous, a destroyer of sacrifices and the like. / To what place has he gone, and how can that place be known by me?

16.336.s:
kathaṃ tasya kriyā kāryā hatasya brāhmaṇaiḥ kila ..
kathaṃ gatirbhavettasya yajñadānakriyābalāt .. 177 ..
16.336.d:
कथं तस्य क्रिया कार्या हतस्य ब्राह्मणैः किल ..
कथं गतिर्भवेत्तस्य यज्ञदानक्रियाबलात् .. 177 ..
16.336.m: How can rites be performed for him who was slain by the brahmins? / How might he attain a [good] destiny through the power of sacrifices, gifts, and rituals?”

16.336.s:
ityeva ciṃtayā tasya nāradobhyājagāma ha ..
tasyaivamāsanaṃ dattvā praṇipatya ca pṛṣṭavān .. 178 ..
16.336.d:
इत्येव चिंतया तस्य नारदोभ्याजगाम ह ..
तस्यैवमासनं दत्त्वा प्रणिपत्य च पृष्टवान् .. 178 ..
16.336.m: While he was reflecting in this manner, Nārada arrived. / Offering him a seat and bowing down, he questioned him:

16.336.s:
bhagavansarvalokasya jānāsi tvaṃ śubhāśubham ..
pitā mama durācāro devabrāhmaṇaniṃdakaḥ .. 179 ..
16.336.d:
भगवन्सर्वलोकस्य जानासि त्वं शुभाशुभम् ..
पिता मम दुराचारो देवब्राह्मणनिंदकः .. 179 ..
16.336.m: “O venerable one, you know the good and evil of all the world. / My father was of wicked conduct, a reviler of gods and brahmins;

16.336.s:
svakarmaṇā hato vipraiḥ paralokamavāptavān ..
kasmiṃsthāne gatastātaḥ śvabhraṃ vā svargameva ca .. 7.1.336.180 ..
16.336.d:
स्वकर्मणा हतो विप्रैः परलोकमवाप्तवान् ..
कस्मिंस्थाने गतस्तातः श्वभ्रं वा स्वर्गमेव च .. 7.1.336.180 ..
16.336.m: slain by the brahmins on account of his own deeds, he has reached the other world. / To what place has my father gone—to a pit or to heaven?”

16.336.s:
tato'bravīnnāradastu jñātvā divyena cakṣuṣā ..
śṛṇu rājanmahābāho yatra tiṣṭhati te pitā .. 181 ..
16.336.d:
ततोऽब्रवीन्नारदस्तु ज्ञात्वा दिव्येन चक्षुषा ..
शृणु राजन्महाबाहो यत्र तिष्ठति ते पिता .. 181 ..
16.336.m: Then Nārada spoke, having perceived [it] through his divine eye: / “Hear, O mighty-armed king, where your father stays.

16.336.s:
atra deśo marurnāma jalavṛkṣavivarjitaḥ ..
tatra deśe mahāraudre janakaste narottama .. 182 ..
16.336.d:
अत्र देशो मरुर्नाम जलवृक्षविवर्जितः ..
तत्र देशे महारौद्रे जनकस्ते नरोत्तम .. 182 ..
16.336.m: Here there is a desert region named Maru, devoid of water and trees; / in that exceedingly terrible region is your father, O best of men:

16.336.s:
mlecchamadhye samutpanno yakṣmī kuṣṭhasamanvitaḥ ..
ucchiṣṭabhojī mlecchānāṃ kṛmibhiḥ saṃyuto vraṇaiḥ .. .. 183 ..
16.336.d:
म्लेच्छमध्ये समुत्पन्नो यक्ष्मी कुष्ठसमन्वितः ..
उच्छिष्टभोजी म्लेच्छानां कृमिभिः संयुतो व्रणैः .. .. 183 ..
16.336.m: born among mlecchas, suffering from consumption and afflicted with leprosy, / eating the remnants of mlecchas' food, covered with worms and sores.”

16.336.s:
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya nāradasya mahātmanaḥ ..
hāhākāraṃ tataḥ kṛtvā mūrchito nipapāta ha ..184 ..
16.336.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य नारदस्य महात्मनः ..
हाहाकारं ततः कृत्वा मूर्छितो निपपात ह ..184 ..
16.336.m: Hearing those words of the great-souled Nārada, / he cried out in distress and fell into a swoon.

16.336.s:
ciṃtayāmāsa duḥkhārtaḥ kathaṃ kāryaṃ mayā bhavet ..
ityevaṃ ciṃtayānasya matirjātā mahātmanaḥ ..
putraḥ sa kathyate loke pitaraṃ trāyate tu yaḥ .. 185 ..
16.336.d:
चिंतयामास दुःखार्तः कथं कार्यं मया भवेत् ..
इत्येवं चिंतयानस्य मतिर्जाता महात्मनः ..
पुत्रः स कथ्यते लोके पितरं त्रायते तु यः .. 185 ..
16.336.m: Afflicted with sorrow, he thought: “What ought to be done by me?” / As he was reflecting in this manner, the thought arose in the great-souled one: / “He is called a son in the world who delivers his father.

16.336.s:
sa kathaṃ tu mayā tātaḥ pāpānmukto bhaviṣyati ..
evaṃ saṃciṃtya sa tato nāradaṃ paryapṛcchata .. 186 ..
bhagavankathitaṃ sarvaṃ piturmama viceṣṭitam ..
kena tasya bhavenmuktiḥ karmaṇā dvijasattama ..
vratairdānaistapobhirvā tīrthānāṃ yātrayā vada .. 177 ..
16.336.d:
स कथं तु मया तातः पापान्मुक्तो भविष्यति ..
एवं संचिंत्य स ततो नारदं पर्यपृच्छत .. 186 ..
भगवन्कथितं सर्वं पितुर्मम विचेष्टितम् ..
केन तस्य भवेन्मुक्तिः कर्मणा द्विजसत्तम ..
व्रतैर्दानैस्तपोभिर्वा तीर्थानां यात्रया वद .. 177 ..
16.336.m:
How then will my father be freed from sin?” / Reflecting thus, he then asked Nārada:
“O venerable one, the entire condition of my father has been described. / By what action might his liberation be achieved, O best of brahmins? / Tell me: through vows, gifts, austerities, or pilgrimage to sacred fords?”

16.336.s:
.. nārada uvāca .. ..
gaccha rājanpradhānāni tīrthāni manujeśvara ..
pitaraṃ teṣu cānīya tasmādrājanmarusthalāt .. 188 ..
16.336.d:
.. नारद उवाच .. ..
गच्छ राजन्प्रधानानि तीर्थानि मनुजेश्वर ..
पितरं तेषु चानीय तस्माद्राजन्मरुस्थलात् .. 188 ..
16.336.m: Nārada said: / “Go to the principal sacred fords, O king, lord of men, / having brought your father to them from that desert region, O king.

16.336.s:
yatra devāḥ saprabhāvāstīrthāni vimalāni ca ..
tatra gaccha mahārāja tīrthayātrāṃ kuru prabho .. 189 ..
16.336.d:
यत्र देवाः सप्रभावास्तीर्थानि विमलानि च ..
तत्र गच्छ महाराज तीर्थयात्रां कुरु प्रभो .. 189 ..
16.336.m: Where there are powerful gods and spotless sacred fords, / go there, O great king, and make a pilgrimage to the sacred fords, O lord.

16.336.s:
evaṃ hyavitathaṃ viddhi mokṣaste bhavitā pituḥ ..
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ rājā nāradasya mahātmanaḥ ..
sacive bhāramādhāya svarājasya jagāma ha .. 7.1.336.190 ..
16.336.d:
एवं ह्यवितथं विद्धि मोक्षस्ते भविता पितुः ..
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं राजा नारदस्य महात्मनः ..
सचिवे भारमाधाय स्वराजस्य जगाम ह .. 7.1.336.190 ..
16.336.m: Know this as unfailing truth: the liberation of your father will come to pass.” / Hearing those words of the great-souled Nārada, / the king placed the burden of his kingdom upon his minister and set forth.

16.336.s:
sa gatvā marubhūmiṃ tu mlecchamadhye dadarśa ha ..
kuṣṭharogeṇa mahatā kṣayeṇa ca samāvṛtam .. 191 ..
16.336.d:
स गत्वा मरुभूमिं तु म्लेच्छमध्ये ददर्श ह ..
कुष्ठरोगेण महता क्षयेण च समावृतम् .. 191 ..
16.336.m: He went to the desert land and saw [his father] among the Mlecchas, / afflicted by severe leprosy and consumption.

16.336.s:
gavyūtimātraṃ tatraiva śūnyaṃ mānuṣavarjitam ..
evaṃ dṛṣṭvā sa rājā tu saṃtapto vākyamabravīt .. 192 ..
16.336.d:
गव्यूतिमात्रं तत्रैव शून्यं मानुषवर्जितम् ..
एवं दृष्ट्वा स राजा तु संतप्तो वाक्यमब्रवीत् .. 192 ..
16.336.m: For a distance of a gavyūti right there, it was deserted, devoid of humans. / Seeing this, the king was tormented and spoke these words:

16.336.s:
he mleccha rogipuruṣaṃ svagṛhaṃ ca nayāmyaham ..
tatrāhamenaṃ nirujaṃ karomi yadi manyatha .. 193 ..
16.336.d:
हे म्लेच्छ रोगिपुरुषं स्वगृहं च नयाम्यहम् ..
तत्राहमेनं निरुजं करोमि यदि मन्यथ .. 193 ..
16.336.m: "O Mlecchas, I shall take this sick man to my own home. / There I shall make him healthy, if you agree."

16.336.s:
jñātveti sarve te mlecchāḥ puruṣaṃ taṃ dayāparam ..
ūcuḥ praṇatasarvāṃgāḥ śīghra naya jagatpate ..
asmadbhāgyavaśānnātha tvamevātra samāgataḥ .. 194 ..
16.336.d:
ज्ञात्वेति सर्वे ते म्लेच्छाः पुरुषं तं दयापरम् ..
ऊचुः प्रणतसर्वांगाः शीघ्र नय जगत्पते ..
अस्मद्भाग्यवशान्नाथ त्वमेवात्र समागतः .. 194 ..
16.336.m: Understanding this, all those Mlecchas bowed with their entire bodies / and said to that most compassionate man: "Take him quickly, O lord of the world! / By virtue of our good fortune, O protector, you have come here yourself!

16.336.s:
durgaṃdhopahatā lokāstvayā nātha sukhīkṛtāḥ ..
tata ānāyya puruṣāñchibikāvāhanocitān .. 195 ..
16.336.d:
दुर्गंधोपहता लोकास्त्वया नाथ सुखीकृताः ..
तत आनाय्य पुरुषाञ्छिबिकावाहनोचितान् .. 195 ..
16.336.m: The people who were afflicted by the foul odor have been made happy by you, O lord!" / Then, having summoned men suitable for carrying a palanquin,

16.336.s:
tataḥ śrutvā tu vacanaṃ tasya rājño dayāvaham ..
prāpustīrthānyanekāni kedārādīni koṭiśaḥ .. 196 ..
16.336.d:
ततः श्रुत्वा तु वचनं तस्य राज्ञो दयावहम् ..
प्रापुस्तीर्थान्यनेकानि केदारादीनि कोटिशः .. 196 ..
16.336.m: and having heard that compassionate command of the king, / they reached many sacred fords by the millions, beginning with Kedāra.

16.336.s:
yatrayatra sa gaccheta vainyo venena saṃyutaḥ ..
tatra tatraiva tīrthānāmākraṃdaḥ śrūyate mahān.. .. 197 ..
16.336.d:
यत्रयत्र स गच्छेत वैन्यो वेनेन संयुतः ..
तत्र तत्रैव तीर्थानामाक्रंदः श्रूयते महान्.. .. 197 ..
16.336.m: Wherever Vainya went accompanied by Vena, / there, precisely there, a great outcry of the sacred fords was heard:

16.336.s:
hā daiva ripurāyāti asmākaṃ nāśahetave ..
adhunā kva gamiṣyāma iti ciṃtā punaḥpunaḥ..198..
16.336.d:
हा दैव रिपुरायाति अस्माकं नाशहेतवे ..
अधुना क्व गमिष्याम इति चिंता पुनःपुनः..198..
16.336.m: "Alas, fate! An enemy is approaching to cause our destruction! / Where shall we go now?"—thus was their constant anxiety.

16.336.s:
darśanenāpi tasyaiva hāhākāraṃ vidhāya vai.. .
palāyaṃte ca tīrthāni devā naśyaṃti tatkṣaṇāt ..199..
16.336.d:
दर्शनेनापि तस्यैव हाहाकारं विधाय वै.. .
पलायंते च तीर्थानि देवा नश्यंति तत्क्षणात् ..199..
16.336.m: Even at the mere sight of him, raising cries of distress, / the sacred fords flee, and the gods vanish at that very instant.

16.336.s:
evaṃ varṣatrayaṃ rājā tīrthayātrāṃ cakāra vai ..
na tasya muktirdadṛśe tataḥ śokamagātparam ..7.1.336.200..
16.336.d:
एवं वर्षत्रयं राजा तीर्थयात्रां चकार वै ..
न तस्य मुक्तिर्ददृशे ततः शोकमगात्परम् ..7.1.336.200..
16.336.m: In this way the king undertook a pilgrimage to sacred fords for three years; / no liberation was seen for him, and so he fell into supreme grief.

16.336.s:
tatastu preritā bhṛtyāḥ kurukṣetre mahāprabhe ..
yadi vāpi punastatra pāpamuktirbhavettataḥ .. 201 ..
16.336.d:
ततस्तु प्रेरिता भृत्याः कुरुक्षेत्रे महाप्रभे ..
यदि वापि पुनस्तत्र पापमुक्तिर्भवेत्ततः .. 201 ..
16.336.m: Then the servants were sent to the splendid Kurukṣetra, / [thinking] whether his liberation from sin might perhaps take place there.

16.336.s:
gṛhītvā śibikāṃ skandhe kurukṣetre gatāḥ priye ..
tatra nītvā sthāṇutīrthamavatārya ca te gatāḥ .. 202 ..
16.336.d:
गृहीत्वा शिबिकां स्कन्धे कुरुक्षेत्रे गताः प्रिये ..
तत्र नीत्वा स्थाणुतीर्थमवतार्य च ते गताः .. 202 ..
16.336.m: Taking the palanquin upon their shoulders, they went to Kurukṣetra, O dear one; / having carried him there, they set him down at Sthāṇutīrtha and went [to the water].

16.336.s:
tataḥ sa rājā madhyāhne cikīrṣuḥ snānamādarāt ..
tasyaiva tu pitustatra tathā dānāni ṣoḍaśa .. 203 ..
16.336.d:
ततः स राजा मध्याह्ने चिकीर्षुः स्नानमादरात् ..
तस्यैव तु पितुस्तत्र तथा दानानि षोडश .. 203 ..
16.336.m: Then, at midday, that king wished to perform a ritual ablution with devotion / on behalf of that very father of his, and likewise to make sixteen gifts,

16.336.s:
brāhmaṇebhyastathā ditsuḥ śraddhāvānbhāvatatparaḥ ..
tato vāyuścāṃtarikṣa idaṃ vacanamabravīt .. 204 ..
16.336.d:
ब्राह्मणेभ्यस्तथा दित्सुः श्रद्धावान्भावतत्परः ..
ततो वायुश्चांतरिक्ष इदं वचनमब्रवीत् .. 204 ..
16.336.m: desiring to give to the brahmins, faithful and devoted in spirit. / Then the Wind-god from the sky spoke these words:

16.336.s:
mā tāta sāhasaṃ kuryāstīrthaṃ rakṣa prayatnataḥ ..
ayaṃ pāpena ghoreṇa samaṃtātpariveṣṭitaḥ .. 205 ..
16.336.d:
मा तात साहसं कुर्यास्तीर्थं रक्ष प्रयत्नतः ..
अयं पापेन घोरेण समंतात्परिवेष्टितः .. 205 ..
16.336.m: "Do not commit a rash act, my dear; protect the sacred ford with diligence! / This man is surrounded on all sides by terrible sin.

16.336.s:
vedanindāsamācāro brahmahatyāśatairyutaḥ ..
so'yaṃ pāpo durācārastīrthaṃ nāśaṃ nayiṣyati .. 206 ..
16.336.d:
वेदनिन्दासमाचारो ब्रह्महत्याशतैर्युतः ..
सोऽयं पापो दुराचारस्तीर्थं नाशं नयिष्यति .. 206 ..
16.336.m: His practice was censuring the Vedas, and he is burdened with hundreds of slayings of brahmins; / this sinner of vile conduct will bring about the ruin of the sacred ford.

16.336.s:
mā tīrthaṃ nāśaya vibho mahadeno bhaviṣyati ..
etadvāyorvacaḥ śrutvā duḥkhena mahatārditaḥ ..
uvāca śokasaṃtaptaḥ piturduḥkhena duḥkhitaḥ .. 207 ..
16.336.d:
मा तीर्थं नाशय विभो महदेनो भविष्यति ..
एतद्वायोर्वचः श्रुत्वा दुःखेन महतार्दितः ..
उवाच शोकसंतप्तः पितुर्दुःखेन दुःखितः .. 207 ..
16.336.m: Do not destroy the sacred ford, O mighty king; a great sin will arise!" / Hearing these words of the Wind-god, tormented by great pain,

16.336.s:
hā daiveti ca cukrośa ūrddhvabāhuḥ punaḥpunaḥ ..
eṣa ghoreṇa pāpena atīva pariveṣṭitaḥ .. 208 ..
16.336.d:
हा दैवेति च चुक्रोश ऊर्द्ध्वबाहुः पुनःपुनः ..
एष घोरेण पापेन अतीव परिवेष्टितः .. 208 ..
16.336.m: distressed by his father's suffering, burned by grief, he spoke. / He cried out repeatedly, with arms raised high: "Alas, fate! / He is exceedingly enveloped by terrible sin,

16.336.s:
yadanenāpi tīrthena śuddhaḥ karttuṃ na śakyate ..
prāyaścittaṃ kariṣye'haṃ piturarthe na saṃśayaḥ .. 209 ..
16.336.d:
यदनेनापि तीर्थेन शुद्धः कर्त्तुं न शक्यते ..
प्रायश्चित्तं करिष्येऽहं पितुरर्थे न संशयः .. 209 ..
16.336.m: since he cannot be cleansed even by this sacred ford! / I will perform an expiation for my father's sake, without a doubt!"

16.336.s:
evaṃ tasya vacaḥ śrutvā dayāṃ kṛtvā mahīyasīm ..
antarikṣabhavāṃ vācaṃ khecarāḥ punarabruvan .. 7.1.336.210 ..
16.336.d:
एवं तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा दयां कृत्वा महीयसीम् ..
